author: Solao
description: Quest, campaign and gquest targets with a learned mob database and click-to-walk.
script:
--[[
    aw-snd.lua
    Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-04

    Search & Destroy. Target lists for quest, campaign and global quest, a
    learned mob database, and click-to-walk using MudForge's own mapper.

    Three things differ from the Mudlet build this grew out of:

      Quest targets arrive over GMCP (comm.quest carries targ/room/area and
      the completion actions), so quests need no trigger scraping at all.
      Campaign and gquest still do — Aardwolf sends neither over GMCP.

      Walking is findPath, compressed into Aardwolf's own 'run' speedwalks:
      run <dirs>, then any custom exit's commands on their own, then run again.
      walkTo is a last resort only, for when there is no path to compress —
      it single-steps one command per room and ignores the custom exit we
      substituted in.

      The database is one JSON blob through savePluginFile at the default,
      per-world scope. That call is synchronous and returns a boolean, where
      saveTable goes through an async Tauri invoke. Per-world rather than
      app-wide: an Aardwolf mob's room means nothing on another MUD, and the
      world's own file is still shared by every plugin on that world.

    Trigger patterns are carried over verbatim from the Mudlet module, where
    they're proven against live output.
]]

plugin = {
    id          = "aw-snd",
    name        = "Aardwolf Search and Destroy",
    version     = "1.41.1",
    author      = "Solao",
    description = "Quest, campaign and gquest targets with a learned mob database and click-to-walk.",
    settings    = { saveState = true },
}

--[[
    Drop every handler already on a widget event.

    Looked up through _G rather than called by name: a global this build does
    not have throws on the way IN, before pcall can catch anything, so a bare
    reference would take the plugin down on any client that lacks it.
]]
local function drop_handlers(id, event)
    local ok, fn = pcall(function() return _G["unregisterWidgetEvent"] end)
    if ok and type(fn) == "function" then pcall(fn, id, event) end
end


-- @category utilities

local TAG  = "$Y[SnD v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "
local TAGR = "$R[SnD v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "

local DB_FILE  = "snd-mobs.json"

--[[
    The target lists, kept across sessions.

    Campaign and gquest targets only arrive when you type 'cp check' or 'gq
    check', so a reload mid-campaign showed an empty panel until you remembered
    to ask again. Quest state comes over GMCP and is re-requested on login, but
    it lands a second or two late and there's no reason to blink.

    Separate from the mob database because it's small and changes constantly,
    where that one is large and mostly append-only.
]]
local TARGETS_FILE = "snd-targets.json"
local MAX_ROWS = 20000            -- a sighting is ~110 bytes; this is a sane ceiling

--[[
    Icons live in the plugin, not in the shared library or on the repo.

    There are six of them and they never change, so a self-contained plugin
    beats another moving part: no library to deploy, no URL to resolve, works
    offline. The avatars go the other way for the opposite reason — 400 of
    them would be 13MB of base64 to show one picture.

    The block below is regenerated by 'build.sh icons'. Don't hand-edit it.
]]
-- >>> ICONS
local ICONS = {}
ICONS["campaign"] = "data:image/png;base64,"
ICONS["found"] = "data:image/png;base64,"
ICONS["gquest"] = "data:image/png;base64,"
ICONS["hunt"] = "data:image/png;base64,"
ICONS["quest"] = "data:image/png;base64,"
ICONS["target"] = "data:image/png;base64,"
-- <<< ICONS

local function icon(name)
    local d = ICONS[name]
    if type(d) ~= "string" then return "" end
    return '<img class="ico" src="' .. d .. '" alt="">'
end

local widget = nil
local view   = "targets"          -- "targets" | "mobs"
local tab    = "quest"            -- quest | campaign | gquest

--[[
    mobs[key] = { {room, roomid, zone, seen, kills}, ... }

    Keyed on the lowercased mob name. Aardwolf's own 'where' is the first
    thing tried for a lookup; this is the fallback for areas where 'where'
    doesn't work and the record of everywhere something has ever been seen.
]]
local mobs    = {}
local areas   = {}          -- by lowercase NAME
local areaByKey = {}        -- by zone KEY, which is what the map answers with
local keywords = {}

local targets = { quest = {}, campaign = {}, gquest = {} }

--[[
    Whether campaign target lines arriving right now are one listing.

    'cp check' and 'cp info' both print the list you still have to kill, and
    re-running either has to REPLACE what's on the panel rather than add to it —
    add_target appends, so without this a second check shows every target twice
    and a third shows it three times.

    Clearing on the header doesn't cover it. Only 'cp info' prints "The targets
    for this campaign are:"; check strips the preamble down to the targets
    themselves, so its lines used to land straight on top of the previous list.

    So the boundary comes from the lines, not from a header: the first target
    line after a quiet gap starts a new listing and clears, and the rest of the
    burst adds to it. That works whatever either command decides to print above
    the list.
]]
local cpFresh = false       -- inside one burst of campaign target lines
local gqFresh = false       -- ...and the same for a global quest
local gqTmr   = nil
local gqNum   = nil         -- which global quest we are in; several run at once
local gqOffer = nil         -- one declared that we are in range for: {num,lo,hi}
--[[
    A global quest's clocks are in TICKS, not minutes — "Time Remaining: [ 80 ]"
    means eighty ticks. So they are counted down on comm.tick rather than
    converted to seconds against a guessed tick length, which would drift and
    would be an estimate presented as a fact.
]]
local gqLeft  = nil         -- ticks until it ends
local gqStart = nil         -- ticks until it starts, while preparing

--[[
    How long a tick actually is, measured rather than assumed.

    'help tick' says they "average around 30 seconds", which is an average and
    not a constant — so 30 is where this starts and every comm.tick that
    arrives corrects it. Gaps outside 10-120s are thrown away: a reconnect or a
    lagged packet is not a tick length.

    Only ever used to put an approximate wall-clock beside an exact tick count.
    The ticks are the fact; this is the courtesy.
]]
local tickMs   = 30000
local tickLast = nil
local cpTmr   = nil

--[[
    The last mob to die, for tick_off.

    Three sources because Aardwolf's death line varies with the killing blow —
    'An ugly harpy is DEAD!!' one round and 'A filthy harpy collapses as the
    life is hammered out of her. She is DEAD!' the next, where the name is
    nowhere near the word DEAD. The corpse lines are the steady ones: they name
    the mob the same way every time and they arrive in the same breath as the
    kill, which is why the loot tracker reads them too.

    All three land BEFORE the campaign confirmation, so by the time that fires
    this holds the right name.
]]
local lastDead = ""

local quest   = { targ = "" }     -- targ, room, area, deadline, readyAt, turnin
local camp    = {}                -- deadline, needLevel

local dirty = false               -- unsaved sightings
local tdirty = false              -- unsaved target lists

local cfg = {
    scan    = true,               -- learn mobs from room descriptions
    rewrite = true,               -- turn 'cp check' into a clickable list
    hidedone = false,             -- drop finished targets instead of listing them
}

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- helpers. every one of these exists because of something the Lua-to-JS
-- boundary does differently; see the notes in aw-chat.lua and aw-portrait.lua
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function str(v)
    if type(v) ~= "string" then return nil end
    if v == "" or v == "undefined" or v == "null" then return nil end
    return v
end

--[[
    A real number, or nil.

    type(x) == "number" is not enough: NaN is a number and rendered as
    "NaN min left". NaN is the only value that isn't equal to itself, which
    is what the second test is for.
]]
--[[
    Seconds as M:SS. The MUD deals in whole minutes, so a live clock has to
    interpolate between packets — which is the point: 12 minutes sitting
    static for sixty seconds tells you nothing, 11:59 ticking does.
]]
local function clock(sec)
    if type(sec) ~= "number" or sec < 0 then sec = 0 end

    local m = math.floor(sec / 60)
    local r = math.floor(sec - (m * 60))

    return m .. ":" .. (r < 10 and ("0" .. r) or tostring(r))
end

local function num(v)
    local n = tonumber(v)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return nil end
    if n ~= n then return nil end
    return n
end

local function gmcp_get(names)
    for _, name in ipairs(names) do
        local data = getGMCPData(name)
        if type(data) == "table" then return data end
    end
    return nil
end

-- args arrive either 0-indexed from JS or as the raw string
local function argv(args)
    local out = {}

    if type(args) == "string" then
        local cur = ""
        for i = 1, string.len(args) do
            local c = string.sub(args, i, i)
            if c == " " or c == "\t" then
                if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur); cur = "" end
            else
                cur = cur .. c
            end
        end
        if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur) end
        return out
    end

    if type(args) ~= "table" then return out end

    local i = 0
    while args[i] ~= nil do
        table.insert(out, tostring(args[i]))
        i = i + 1
    end

    if #out == 0 then
        for _, v in ipairs(args) do table.insert(out, tostring(v)) end
    end

    return out
end

-- trigger callbacks hand over something that isn't reliably a string
--[[
    The line a trigger matched.

    The official guide settles the signature: a trigger callback receives
    (captures, line, wildcards, rawLine) — captures FIRST, the line second.
    This used to sniff the arguments for the first thing that looked like text,
    which happened to work only because a substring trigger puts the whole line
    in captures[1]. A regex trigger with capture groups would have handed it a
    capture instead and every pattern below would have been matching against
    the wrong string.

    Takes both and prefers the documented one, falling back to the old
    behaviour so a runtime that disagrees doesn't break every trigger at once.
]]
-- your own name, lowercased, or nil while GMCP has not said yet
local function my_name()
    local b = gmcp_get({ "char.base", "Char.Base" })
    local n = b and b.name

    if type(n) == "string" and n ~= "" and n ~= "undefined" then
        return string.lower(n)
    end
    return nil
end

--[[
    Capture n, falling back to re-reading the line only if the captures are not
    there. The wildcards table is keyed by the STRING "1" and has no index base
    to get wrong; captures may arrive 0- or 1-based, so the base is worked out
    once rather than guessed per lookup.
]]
local function cap3(c, w, n, line)
    if type(w) == "table" and type(w[tostring(n)]) == "string" then
        return w[tostring(n)]
    end

    if type(c) == "table" then
        local base = (type(c[0]) == "string") and 0 or 1
        local v = c[n - 1 + base]
        if type(v) == "string" then return v end
    end

    return ""
end

local function as_text(captures, line)
    if type(line) == "string" and line ~= "" then return line end

    -- fallback: substring mode leaves the whole line in the first capture
    if type(captures) == "string" and captures ~= "" then return captures end

    if type(captures) == "table" then
        for _, k in ipairs({ "line", "text", "raw", "match", "matched" }) do
            if type(captures[k]) == "string" and captures[k] ~= "" then
                return captures[k]
            end
        end
        for n = 0, 2 do
            if type(captures[n]) == "string" and captures[n] ~= "" then
                return captures[n]
            end
        end
    end

    return nil
end

local function esc(s)
    if type(s) ~= "string" then return "" end
    s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
    s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
    s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
    s = string.gsub(s, '"', """)
    return s
end

local function trim(s)
    if type(s) ~= "string" then return "" end

    local a, b = 1, string.len(s)
    while a <= b and string.sub(s, a, a) == " " do a = a + 1 end
    while b >= a and string.sub(s, b, b) == " " do b = b - 1 end
    return string.sub(s, a, b)
end

local function commas(n)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return "--" end

    local s, out, count = tostring(math.floor(n)), "", 0
    for i = string.len(s), 1, -1 do
        out = string.sub(s, i, i) .. out
        count = count + 1
        if count % 3 == 0 and i > 1 then out = "," .. out end
    end
    return out
end

local function count(t)
    local n = 0
    if type(t) ~= "table" then return 0 end
    for _ in pairs(t) do n = n + 1 end
    return n
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- database
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function mob_key(name)
    return string.lower(trim(name or ""))
end

--[[
    What the MUD will actually accept as a target.

    Aardwolf's own commands take keywords, and the leading article isn't one:
    'hunt a chilling silence' returns "No one in this area by the name" while
    'hunt chilling silence' works. Applies to hunt, kill and where alike.
]]
local function huntable(name)
    local n = trim(name or "")

    for _, art in ipairs({ "a ", "an ", "the ", "A ", "An ", "The " }) do
        if string.sub(n, 1, string.len(art)) == art then
            return trim(string.sub(n, string.len(art) + 1))
        end
    end

    return n
end

--[[
    Record a sighting. Same mob in the same room bumps the counter rather
    than adding a row — the database is "where has this ever been", not a log.
]]
local function see(name, room, roomid, zone, killed)
    local key = mob_key(name)
    if key == "" then return end

    local list = mobs[key]
    if type(list) ~= "table" then
        list = {}
        mobs[key] = list
    end

    for _, r in ipairs(list) do
        if r.roomid == roomid or (roomid == 0 and r.room == room) then
            r.seen = (tonumber(r.seen) or 0) + 1
            if killed then r.kills = (tonumber(r.kills) or 0) + 1 end
            dirty = true
            return
        end
    end

    table.insert(list, {
        room   = room or "",
        roomid = tonumber(roomid) or 0,
        zone   = zone or "",
        seen   = 1,
        kills  = killed and 1 or 0,
    })
    dirty = true
end

local function rows()
    local n = 0
    for _, list in pairs(mobs) do n = n + #list end
    return n
end

--[[
    Data that survives a reinstall.

    saveTable and savePluginFile are both scoped to the plugin, and removing
    one takes its rows with it — which is exactly how every update to these
    plugins is installed. It is why the mob database re-seeds from the Mudlet
    dump every time and why the target lists came back empty.

    World variables aren't tied to the plugin. The small things go there
    outright; the mob database is mirrored only if the store will take it,
    since it runs to hundreds of kilobytes and nothing documents a limit.
]]
local function keep(name, t)
    local out = {}

    for k, v in pairs(t) do
        local kind = type(v)
        if kind == "string" then
            table.insert(out, '"' .. tostring(k) .. '":"'
                .. string.gsub(string.gsub(v, "\\", ""), '"', "") .. '"')
        elseif kind == "number" or kind == "boolean" then
            table.insert(out, '"' .. tostring(k) .. '":' .. tostring(v))
        end
    end

    pcall(function() setVariable(name, "{" .. table.concat(out, ",") .. "}") end)
end

local function keep_raw(name, blob)
    local ok = pcall(function() setVariable(name, blob) end)
    if not ok then return false end

    -- written is not the same as stored; a size cap would fail silently
    local rok, back = pcall(function() return getVariable(name) end)
    return rok and type(back) == "string" and string.len(back) == string.len(blob)
end

local function recall(name)
    local ok, raw = pcall(function() return getVariable(name) end)
    if not ok or type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return nil end
    return raw
end

--[[
    Per-world, which is the default scope.

    These were written with scope "global" — one namespace shared by every
    character on every world. A database of Aardwolf mobs has no business
    being visible on a different MUD, and the default store is that world's
    own file: isolated between worlds, still shared by every plugin on the
    same one, so anything that wants to read this can.

    read_world() falls back to the old app-wide copy once, so nothing already
    collected disappears the day the scope changes.
]]
local function read_world(file)
    local raw = loadPluginFile(file)
    if type(raw) == "string" and raw ~= "" then return raw end

    --[[
        The old app-wide copy, read by hand rather than through this function.

        A blanket rewrite of loadPluginFile(x, "global") -> read_world(x)
        caught this line too, so read_world called itself and every load ended
        in 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' before a single line of the
        plugin ran.
    ]]
    local old = loadPluginFile(file, "global")
    if type(old) == "string" and old ~= "" then
        pcall(savePluginFile, file, old)
        return old
    end

    return nil
end

local function save_db()
    if not dirty then return end

    local out = {}
    for key, list in pairs(mobs) do
        for _, r in ipairs(list) do
            table.insert(out, '{"m":"' .. string.gsub(key, '"', '')
                .. '","r":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(r.room), '"', '')
                .. '","i":' .. tostring(r.roomid)
                .. ',"z":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(r.zone), '"', '')
                .. '","s":' .. tostring(r.seen)
                .. ',"k":' .. tostring(r.kills) .. '}')
        end
    end

    --[[
        Hand-built JSON. json.encode exists but this walks a table of a few
        thousand rows and the encoder's behaviour on nested arrays through the
        transpiler is exactly the sort of thing that has bitten before.
    ]]
    local blob = "[" .. table.concat(out, ",") .. "]"

    if savePluginFile(DB_FILE, blob) then
        dirty = false
    end

    keep_raw(DB_FILE, blob)
end

local function load_db()
    local raw = read_world(DB_FILE)

    -- the plugin's own file is gone after a reinstall; the variable isn't
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then raw = recall(DB_FILE) end
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return false end

    local ok, data = pcall(json.decode, raw)
    if not ok or type(data) ~= "table" then return false end

    local n = 0
    for _, r in pairs(data) do
        if type(r) == "table" and str(r.m) then
            local key = r.m
            if type(mobs[key]) ~= "table" then mobs[key] = {} end
            table.insert(mobs[key], {
                room   = r.r or "",
                roomid = tonumber(r.i) or 0,
                zone   = r.z or "",
                seen   = tonumber(r.s) or 1,
                kills  = tonumber(r.k) or 0,
            })
            n = n + 1
        end
    end

    return n > 0
end

--[[
    Targets and quest clocks, written out whenever they change.

    Hand-built JSON for the same reason as the mob database: this crosses the
    Lua-to-JavaScript boundary and an encoder's behaviour on nested arrays is
    exactly the kind of thing that has bitten before. Reading uses json.decode,
    which is proven by the database above.

    The clocks are stored as the epochs they expire at, so a stale one simply
    reads as expired rather than as time you don't have.
]]
local function save_targets()
    local parts = {}

    for _, kind in ipairs({ "quest", "campaign", "gquest" }) do
        -- renamed off a file-scope name: shadowing one can fail the whole
        -- plugin load. See NOTES 9b.
        local out = {}

        for _, t in ipairs(targets[kind] or {}) do
            table.insert(out, '{"m":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(t.mob), '"', "")
                .. '","a":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(t.area or ""), '"', "")
                .. '","n":' .. tostring(tonumber(t.need) or 1)
                .. ',"g":' .. tostring(tonumber(t.got) or 0)
                .. ',"d":' .. (t.done and "true" or "false") .. "}")
        end

        table.insert(parts, '"' .. kind .. '":[' .. table.concat(out, ",") .. "]")
    end

    table.insert(parts, '"q":{'
        .. '"targ":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(quest.targ or ""), '"', "") .. '"'
        .. ',"room":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(quest.room or ""), '"', "") .. '"'
        .. ',"area":"' .. string.gsub(tostring(quest.area or ""), '"', "") .. '"'
        .. ',"deadline":' .. tostring(num(quest.deadline) or 0)
        .. ',"readyAt":' .. tostring(num(quest.readyAt) or 0)
        .. ',"turnin":' .. (quest.turnin == true and "true" or "false")
        .. "}")

    local blob = "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
    savePluginFile(TARGETS_FILE, blob)
    keep_raw(TARGETS_FILE, blob)
end

local function load_targets()
    local raw = read_world(TARGETS_FILE)
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then raw = recall(TARGETS_FILE) end
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return end

    local ok, data = pcall(json.decode, raw)
    if not ok or type(data) ~= "table" then return end

    for _, kind in ipairs({ "quest", "campaign", "gquest" }) do
        -- renamed off a file-scope name: shadowing one can fail the whole
        -- plugin load. See NOTES 9b.
        local list = data[kind]
        if type(list) == "table" then
            targets[kind] = {}
            for _, r in pairs(list) do
                if type(r) == "table" and str(r.m) then
                    table.insert(targets[kind], {
                        mob  = r.m,
                        area = r.a or "",
                        need = tonumber(r.n) or 1,
                        got  = tonumber(r.g) or 0,
                        done = r.d == true,
                    })
                end
            end
        end
    end

    local q = data.q
    if type(q) == "table" then
        quest.targ   = str(q.targ)
        quest.room   = str(q.room)
        quest.area   = str(q.area)
        quest.turnin = q.turnin == true

        -- zero means "nothing stored", not "expired a moment ago"
        local dl, ra = num(q.deadline), num(q.readyAt)
        if dl and dl > 0 then quest.deadline = dl end
        if ra and ra > 0 then quest.readyAt = ra end
    end
end

--[[
    First run only: pull in the sightings carried over from the Mudlet
    profile. The library is generated locally and never committed, so a fresh
    install simply starts empty and learns.
]]
--[[
    Area names, runto keywords and mob-keyword exceptions. Cheap, static, and
    needed on every load — unlike the sightings, which are saved once and then
    grown.
]]
local function seed_reference()
    local ok, s = pcall(require, "snd-seed")
    if not ok or type(s) ~= "table" then return end

    for _, a in ipairs(s.areas or {}) do
        if str(a.name) then areas[string.lower(a.name)] = a end
        -- the map answers with the zone KEY ('gilda'), which is not something
        -- to put in front of a player; this is how it becomes a name
        if str(a.key) then areaByKey[string.lower(a.key)] = a end
    end

    for _, k in ipairs(s.keywords or {}) do
        if str(k.mob) then keywords[mob_key(k.mob)] = k.keyword end
    end
end

local function seed_mobs()
    local ok, s = pcall(require, "snd-seed")
    if not ok or type(s) ~= "table" then return 0 end

    local n = 0

    for _, m in ipairs(s.mobs or {}) do
        local key = mob_key(m.mob)
        if key ~= "" then
            if type(mobs[key]) ~= "table" then mobs[key] = {} end
            table.insert(mobs[key], {
                room   = m.room or "",
                roomid = tonumber(m.roomid) or 0,
                zone   = m.zone or "",
                seen   = tonumber(m.seen) or 1,
                kills  = tonumber(m.kills) or 0,
            })
            n = n + 1
        end
    end

    if n > 0 then dirty = true end
    return n
end

--[[
    Everywhere a mob has been seen, best first.

    Matches on substring so 'wolf' finds 'a dire wolf', which is how you
    actually type a target — and sorts by sightings so the room it usually
    lives in comes before the one it wandered into once.
]]
local function where(needle)
    local q = mob_key(needle)
    if q == "" then return {} end

    local hits = {}

    for key, list in pairs(mobs) do
        if string.find(key, q, 1, true) then
            for _, r in ipairs(list) do
                table.insert(hits, {
                    mob = key, room = r.room, roomid = r.roomid,
                    zone = r.zone, seen = r.seen, kills = r.kills,
                })
            end
        end
    end

    table.sort(hits, function(a, b)
        if a.seen ~= b.seen then return a.seen > b.seen end
        return a.mob < b.mob
    end)

    return hits
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- walking
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    The MUD's own runto.

    'runto' takes the area NAME directly — 'runto eternal autumn' works — so
    the keyword is a nicety, not a requirement. An earlier version insisted on
    finding a keyword first and refused with "no runto keyword" for an area
    the player could reach by typing it themselves, which is the worst way to
    be wrong.

    A known keyword is still preferred when we have one: it's shorter and
    unambiguous where two areas share words. Otherwise the name goes as-is and
    the MUD decides.
]]
--[[
    What area a ROOM is in, asked of the client's map.

    'cp check' does not always name an area. For this campaign it named a room
    every single time:

        You still have to kill * a jotun (A Mountain Path)
        You still have to kill * a small rat (Academy Basement Hallway)

    which the panel took at face value and drew as the area — so the row said
    'A Mountain Path', found no such area, and coloured itself unknown with no
    runto. The campaign help says both forms happen: a target shows "either the
    target's name with area location, or just a room name".

    Our own sightings database can't help here — none of those rooms are in it,
    they're newbie rooms nobody imported. The mapper can: it holds every room
    you have ever walked, with the area each one belongs to.

    Answers are cached, including the misses, because this runs per row per
    repaint and a search that failed once will fail the same way all session.
    Nothing is cached before the map is warm, though — that would freeze a
    'don't know' in place for the rest of the session over a lookup that was
    only ever going to work later.
]]
--[[
    What each GO button means, by row.

    The button carries an INDEX, not a payload. Packing '<vnum>:<area>' into
    one attribute and splitting it on the way back gave the MUD
    'runto 15491:sennarre' — the two halves arrived joined, and it does not
    much matter which layer did it when the answer is to stop encoding two
    things as one string. An integer cannot be mis-split.

    Rebuilt on every render, in the order the rows are drawn, so an index is
    only ever read against the list it was drawn from.
]]
local goRows = {}
-- runto rows carry the MOB as well as the area: arriving is only half of it,
-- the other half is asking the MUD where the thing actually is
local runRows = {}

local roomArea = {}

-- what level you are, for picking between rooms that share a name
local function my_level()
    local st = gmcp_get({ "char.status", "Char.Status" })
    local n  = st and tonumber(st.level)
    if n then return n end

    local b = gmcp_get({ "char.base", "Char.Base" })
    n = b and tonumber(b.level)
    return n
end

--[[
    How wrong an area is for you, in levels. 0 means it fits.

    Room names repeat all over Aardwolf — 'A Mountain Path' exists in a dozen
    areas — and taking the first match got a level 2 campaign target placed in
    Gilda And The Dragon, which is 120-140. The seed knows every area's level
    range, so the candidate that fits the character wins.
]]
--[[
    How badly an area fits your level. Lower is better.

    An area we know NOTHING about is not a perfect fit — it used to score 0,
    the same as one whose range you sit in the middle of. Generic room names
    exist in a dozen areas ('Light forest', 'Small Privy', 'On a Rugged
    Trail'), so every candidate tied at zero and whichever pairs() yielded
    first won. That is how 'Light forest' became Giant's Pet Store.

    Not infinite, because a real answer with no level data still beats no
    answer at all — just never a known-and-fitting one.
]]
local UNKNOWN_MISS = 500

local function level_miss(rec, lvl)
    if type(rec) ~= "table" or not lvl then return UNKNOWN_MISS end

    local lo, hi = tonumber(rec.minlvl), tonumber(rec.maxlvl)
    if not (lo and hi) then return UNKNOWN_MISS end

    if lvl < lo then return lo - lvl end
    if lvl > hi then return lvl - hi end
    return 0
end

--[[
    Which area a ROOM NAME belongs to.

    A campaign names the room and NOT the area — 'You still have to kill * an
    old woman dressed in black (Captain's Office)' — and plenty of areas have a
    Captain's Office. Level fit alone picked Kerofk, sent you there, and there
    was no old woman in it.

    So where we have SEEN the mob wins over where its level says it should be.
    A sighting is evidence; a level range is a guess that fits a hundred areas.
    Level fit is still the tiebreak when we have never seen the thing, which
    for a campaign in an area nobody has walked is the normal case — and 'where'
    on arrival is what turns that into evidence for next time.
]]
local function area_of_room(name, seenZones)
    local n = trim(name or "")
    if n == "" then return nil end

    -- the cache has to know which mob's sightings shaped the answer, or the
    -- first lookup pins 'Captain's Office' for every mob after it
    local key = string.lower(n)
    if type(seenZones) == "table" then
        local mark = {}
        for z in pairs(seenZones) do table.insert(mark, z) end
        table.sort(mark)
        if #mark > 0 then key = key .. "|" .. table.concat(mark, ",") end
    end

    local hit = roomArea[key]
    if hit ~= nil then
        if hit == false then return nil end
        return hit
    end

    --[[
        type() before pcall, every time. pcall does NOT protect a call to a
        name that doesn't exist — resolving the global throws before pcall ever
        sees it, which is how the missing 'emit' took a whole plugin down.
    ]]
    if type(isMapReady) ~= "function" or type(searchRoom) ~= "function"
        or type(getRoomArea) ~= "function" then
        return nil
    end

    if not isMapReady() then return nil end

    local ok, rooms = pcall(searchRoom, n, true)
    if not ok or type(rooms) ~= "table" then
        roomArea[key] = false
        return nil
    end

    --[[
        searchRoom answers { vnum = name }. Every room that really carries this
        name is a candidate; the one in an area that fits your level wins, and
        ties go to whichever came first.
    ]]
    --[[
        No level yet, no answer yet.

        char.status arrives a moment after the plugin loads, and a pick made in
        that gap is a coin toss between areas a hundred levels apart. Caching it
        would then keep that coin toss for the rest of the session, so this
        declines to answer rather than answering badly. render() runs again on
        the next GMCP update and by then there is a level.
    ]]
    local lvl = my_level()
    if not lvl then return nil end

    local best, bestMiss = nil, nil
    local tied = false

    for vnum, rname in pairs(rooms) do
        if string.lower(trim(tostring(rname))) == key then
            local ok2, zone = pcall(getRoomArea, tonumber(vnum) or vnum)
            if ok2 and type(zone) == "string" and trim(zone) ~= "" then
                zone = trim(zone)

                local rec  = areaByKey[string.lower(zone)]
                local miss = level_miss(rec, lvl)

                --[[
                    Seen there beats fits-the-level. Kept as a big negative
                    rather than a separate branch so the existing comparison
                    still does the work, and two seen candidates still sort by
                    level fit between themselves.
                ]]
                if type(seenZones) == "table" and seenZones[string.lower(zone)] then
                    miss = miss - 1000000
                end

                --[[
                    Ties break on the lowest vnum, and a tie is REMEMBERED.

                    Arbitrary order is not a decision, and a coin toss printed
                    as fact is what sent us to three wrong areas in a row. The
                    flag lets the row say it is unsure.
                ]]
                local vn = tonumber(vnum) or 0

                if best and miss == bestMiss then
                    tied = true
                    if vn > 0 and vn < (tonumber(best.vnum) or 1e12) then
                        best.key  = zone
                        best.name = (rec and str(rec.name)) or zone
                        best.vnum = vn
                    end
                end

                if not best or miss < bestMiss then
                    if best and miss < bestMiss then tied = false end
                    -- the vnum too: this is the exact room the MUD named, which
                    -- is a better place to walk to than anywhere we merely
                    -- remember seeing the mob
                    best     = { key  = zone,
                                 name = (rec and str(rec.name)) or zone,
                                 vnum = tonumber(vnum) or vnum }
                    bestMiss = miss
                end
            end
        end
    end

    -- a tie means we picked one of several equally good answers, which the
    -- row needs to know so it does not present a coin toss as a fact
    if best then best.guess = tied end

    roomArea[key] = best or false
    return best
end

--[[
    A mapper list, as a plain Lua array.

    The guide says these 0-indexed arrays can be walked with ipairs, and in
    this build they cannot. The keys arrive as STRINGS, so ipairs looks up the
    NUMBER 1, finds nothing, and stops before the first element — silently, and
    an empty result reads exactly like "no rooms matched".

    That is the same reason the probe needs at(): v[0] with a number misses and
    v["0"] hits. Measured, not assumed — searchRooms hands back three rooms and
    an ipairs loop over them yields none.

    Indexed walk first and in order, because directions must stay in order.
    pairs is the last resort and only when nothing was found positionally, so
    its undefined order can never scramble a route.
]]
local function mapl(v)
    local out = {}
    if type(v) ~= "table" then return out end

    local i = 0
    while true do
        local e = v[i]
        if e == nil then e = v[tostring(i)] end
        if e == nil then break end
        table.insert(out, e)
        i = i + 1
    end
    if #out > 0 then return out end

    -- a real 1-indexed Lua table: the sim builds them, and so does anything
    -- that has already been through here once
    i = 1
    while true do
        local e = v[i]
        if e == nil then e = v[tostring(i)] end
        if e == nil then break end
        table.insert(out, e)
        i = i + 1
    end
    if #out > 0 then return out end

    for _, e in pairs(v) do table.insert(out, e) end
    return out
end

--[[
    A field off a mapper table, whatever the keys really are.

    findPath's result printed { found=false  distance=0 } and reading .found
    off that same table still gave undefined — pairs() sees keys that dot
    access does not. Room tables read fine by name, but one silent nil here
    means the area filter below never matches and GO quietly stops working, so
    it is not worth betting on.
]]
local function fld(t, name)
    if type(t) ~= "table" then return nil end
    if t[name] ~= nil then return t[name] end

    for k, v in pairs(t) do
        if tostring(k) == name then return v end
    end
    return nil
end

--[[
    The room the MUD named, inside the area the MUD named.

    Quests hand over BOTH — data.room and data.area — and this used to keep
    only the area and let area_of_room infer the rest from the room name by
    level fit. 'The Common Room' exists in dortmund, shouggoth and bootcamp;
    guessing between three when the MUD already said which is how GO kept
    walking out of the area.

        searchRooms(query, opts?) -> array of room tables
        opts = { exact = false, caseSensitive = false }

    It is map-wide with no area option, so the filter is ours. exact is
    whole-name but still case-insensitive, which is why dortmund's lowercase
    'The common room' comes back too — compare the AREA, not the spelling.

    Nearest wins when one area repeats a room name; getDistance answers -1 for
    unreachable, which must not be read as "very close".
]]
local roomInArea = {}

local function room_in_area(roomName, areaName)
    local n = trim(roomName or "")
    local a = string.lower(trim(areaName or ""))
    if n == "" or a == "" then return nil end

    --[[
        Cached, because this sits in render().

        searchRooms scans the whole map and getDistance is a PATHFIND, not a
        lookup — the doc is explicit that it honours locks and weights. Running
        both on every redraw, and redraws happen on every quest packet, is a
        full-map scan a few times a minute to answer a question whose answer is
        map data and does not change.
    ]]
    local ck  = a .. "|" .. string.lower(n)
    local hit = roomInArea[ck]
    if hit ~= nil then
        if hit == false then return nil end
        return hit
    end

    -- type() before pcall: resolving a name this build lacks throws on the way
    -- in, before pcall can catch it
    if type(isMapReady) ~= "function" or type(searchRooms) ~= "function" then return nil end
    if not isMapReady() then return nil end

    local ok, rooms = pcall(searchRooms, n, { exact = true })
    if not ok or type(rooms) ~= "table" then return nil end

    --[[
        Candidates first, distances only if there is a choice to make.

        One room in the area carries the name nearly every time, and that is
        the answer no matter how far off it is — measuring the distance to the
        only option is a pathfind spent to confirm what was already decided.
    ]]
    local hits = {}

    for _, r in ipairs(mapl(rooms)) do
        local zone = trim(tostring(fld(r, "area") or fld(r, "zone") or ""))
        local vn   = tonumber(fld(r, "num"))
        if vn and string.lower(zone) == a then table.insert(hits, vn) end
    end

    if #hits == 0 then
        roomInArea[ck] = false
        return nil
    end

    if #hits == 1 then
        roomInArea[ck] = hits[1]
        return hits[1]
    end

    --[[
        Genuinely ambiguous, so pay for it — and do NOT cache the winner. It is
        the nearest one from where you are standing, which is a different room
        once you have walked somewhere else.
    ]]
    local from = nil
    if type(getPlayerRoom) == "function" then
        local okp, v = pcall(getPlayerRoom)
        if okp then
            v = tonumber(v)
            if v and v > 0 then from = v end
        end
    end

    if not from or type(getDistance) ~= "function" then return hits[1] end

    --[[
        A NUMBER to beat, not a nil to test against.

        `bestDist == nil` is not a guard you can rely on here: an uninitialised
        local is `undefined`, and `undefined == nil` is false, so the guard
        never fires and nothing is ever assigned. The probe returned the word
        "undefined" as a room number for exactly this.
    ]]
    local best     = hits[1]
    local bestDist = 1e9

    for _, vn in ipairs(hits) do
        local okd, dist = pcall(getDistance, from, vn)
        dist = okd and tonumber(dist) or nil
        -- -1 is unreachable, which must never read as "very close"
        if dist and dist >= 0 and dist < bestDist then
            best, bestDist = vn, dist
        end
    end

    return best
end

local function area_key(name)
    local n = string.lower(trim(name or ""))
    if n == "" then return nil end

    local a = areas[n]
    if type(a) == "table" and str(a.key) then return a.key end

    -- names differ in case and punctuation between sources; a substring hit
    -- is nearly always the same place
    for key, rec in pairs(areas) do
        if string.find(key, n, 1, true) or string.find(n, key, 1, true) then
            if type(rec) == "table" and str(rec.key) then return rec.key end
        end
    end

    return nil
end

--[[
    When our own runto was sent, so the ambiguity list below can tell the MUD's
    answer to us apart from a line that merely looks like one.
]]
local runtoAt = 0

local function runto(area)
    local name = trim(area or "")
    if name == "" then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "no area to run to.")
        return false
    end

    --[[
        The keyword when we know one, and the article is never part of it.

            [SnD] runto the caboose
            The is not an area keyword or a find location in this area.

        'runto' takes ONE token, so it read 'the' and stopped — and it says so
        in those words, which is how this was found. huntable() already strips
        a/an/the for hunt and kill; the same applies here.
    ]]
    local target = area_key(name)

    if target == nil then
        local bare = huntable(name)
        target = area_key(bare) or string.lower(bare)
    end

    utilprint(TAG .. "runto " .. target)
    runtoAt = getCurrentTime()
    send("runto " .. target)
    return true
end

--[[
    Two areas can share a name.

        > runto school of horror
        Sohtwo       - The School of Horror
        Soh          - The School of Horror

    The MUD answers with the keywords instead of moving, and you are expected
    to read them and retype one. So each becomes a link that sends it.

    The pattern is deliberately broad — a word, a dash, a name — which is why
    it only does anything within a few seconds of a runto WE sent. Outside that
    window it is any number of ordinary lines, and gagging those would be a
    disaster.
]]
local function on_runto_choice(captures, line)
    if (getCurrentTime() - runtoAt) > 3000 then return end

    local text = as_text(captures, line)
    if type(text) ~= "string" then return end

    local at = string.find(text, " - ", 1, true)
    if not at then return end

    local key  = trim(string.sub(text, 1, at - 1))
    local name = trim(string.sub(text, at + 3))

    if key == "" or name == "" or string.find(key, " ", 1, true) then return end

    hyperlink("$Y" .. key .. "$w  " .. name, "runto " .. key,
        { hint = "run to " .. name })

    -- ours replaces it, rather than printing beside it
    return false
end

--[[
    Walk to a room if the map knows it, otherwise let the MUD run us to the
    area. A recorded room id is no use when the mapper has never been there —
    which is common for a campaign target three continents away.
]]
--[[
    Auto-hunt. Follows the MUD's own hunt skill one room at a time: hunt,
    read the direction, move, hunt again, until the mob is in the room.

    Worth having even with a mapped room id, because hunt works in areas the
    map has never seen — and it follows a mob that moves, which a speedwalk
    to a remembered room does not.

    Patterns are carried over verbatim from the Mudlet module. They encode
    things learned the hard way: the arrival line has to be checked against
    the mob we asked for, because the MUD prints "X is here!" for every mob in
    the room; and under 85% hunt skill the MUD hedges and the direction is a
    guess worth refusing rather than following three areas away.
]]
local hunt = { mob = nil, steps = 0, lastdir = nil, opening = false, trig = {}, timer = nil }

local MAX_STEPS = 120

local function hunt_untrig()
    for _, id in pairs(hunt.trig) do removeTrigger(id) end
    hunt.trig = {}
end

local function hunt_stop(why, found)
    hunt_untrig()

    local was = hunt.mob
    hunt.mob, hunt.steps, hunt.lastdir, hunt.opening = nil, 0, nil, false

    if not was then return end

    if found then
        utilprint(TAG .. "found " .. was .. ".")
    elseif why then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "hunt stopped: " .. why .. ".")
    end
end

local function hunt_arm(pattern, fn)
    table.insert(hunt.trig, addTrigger(pattern, fn, { type = "regex" }))
end

local function hunt_step(dir)
    if not hunt.mob then return end

    hunt.steps = hunt.steps + 1
    if hunt.steps > MAX_STEPS then
        hunt_stop("gave up after " .. MAX_STEPS .. " rooms")
        return
    end

    hunt.lastdir = dir
    send(dir)

    --[[
        Re-hunt a beat later rather than immediately: the move has to resolve
        first, and hunting mid-move gets the previous room's answer.
    ]]
    hunt.timer = setTimeout(function()
        if hunt.mob then send("hunt " .. hunt.mob) end
    end, 400)
end

local function hunt_start(name)
    local mobName = trim(name or "")

    if mobName == "" then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "ah <mob>   ('aha' to cancel)")
        return
    end

    local low = string.lower(mobName)
    if low == "stop" or low == "cancel" or low == "0" then
        hunt_stop("cancelled")
        return
    end

    mobName = huntable(mobName)

    hunt_stop()
    hunt.mob, hunt.steps, hunt.lastdir, hunt.opening = mobName, 0, nil, false
    low = string.lower(mobName)
    utilprint(TAG .. "hunting " .. mobName .. "...")

    -- the two readings that mean the trail is solid
    hunt_arm("^You are confident that .+ passed through here, heading (north|south|east|west|up|down)\\.$",
        function(a, b)
            local line = as_text(a, b) or ""
            local dir  = string.match(line, "heading (north|south|east|west|up|down)")
            if dir then hunt_step(dir) end
        end)

    hunt_arm("^You are (?:almost )?certain that .+ is (north|south|east|west|up|down) from here\\.$",
        function(a, b)
            local line = as_text(a, b) or ""
            local dir  = string.match(line, "is (north|south|east|west|up|down) from here")
            if dir then hunt_step(dir) end
        end)

    --[[
        Arrival. Checked against the mob we asked for: the MUD prints
        "X is here!" for every mob in the room, so an unanchored match stops
        the hunt on whatever happens to be standing next to the target.
        Matched generically and compared here, because building a regex out of
        a MUD-typed name breaks on apostrophes and parentheses.
    ]]
    --[[
        Arrival. The MUD prints "<something> is here!" for every mob in the
        room, so the line has to be both shaped right AND about our target.

        Compare the SUBJECT, not the line. A find() against the whole line
        matches "You couldn't find a path to an obsidian cyclops from here."
        too — which is how a catch got reported on the exact line saying it
        failed. Strip the suffix, strip the article, and compare what's left.

        Explicit index maths rather than string.sub(line, -9): negative indices
        are a stdlib corner and this transpiler has surprised us on those.
    ]]
    hunt_arm("^.+ is here!$", function(a, b)
        local line = as_text(a, b)
        if type(line) ~= "string" then return end

        local cut = string.len(line) - 9
        if cut < 1 or string.sub(line, cut + 1) ~= " is here!" then return end

        local subject = string.lower(huntable(string.sub(line, 1, cut)))
        local back    = string.len(subject) - string.len(low)

        if subject == low or (back > 0 and string.sub(subject, back + 1) == low) then
            hunt_stop(nil, true)
        end
    end)

    -- under 85% hunt skill the direction is a guess; following it is how you
    -- end up three areas away
    hunt_arm("^(?:The trail of .+ is confusing|There are traces of .+ having been here|You have no idea what you're doing)",
        function() hunt_stop("hunt skill too low to trust the trail") end)

    -- a portal needs a command we can't infer
    hunt_arm("^You are (?:almost )?certain that .+ is through .+\\.$",
        function() hunt_stop("the trail goes through a portal — take it yourself") end)
    hunt_arm("^You are confident that .+ passed through here, heading through .+\\.$",
        function() hunt_stop("the trail goes through a portal — take it yourself") end)

    -- a shut door is worth one 'open' in the direction we were already going
    hunt_arm("^The .+ is closed\\.$", function()
        if hunt.lastdir and not hunt.opening then
            hunt.opening = true
            send("open " .. hunt.lastdir)
            hunt_step(hunt.lastdir)
        end
    end)

    --[[
        Refusals. Left-anchored only — a trailing space or a colour reset the
        line handler didn't strip defeats a '$' and the refusal then never
        fires, which leaves the hunt running past the MUD telling it to stop.
        Nothing else on Aardwolf opens with these words, so '^' alone is enough.
    ]]
    hunt_arm("^(?:No one in this area by (?:the name '.+'|that name)\\.|You couldn't find a path to .+ from here\\.|You seem unable to hunt that target for some reason\\.)",
        function() hunt_stop("the MUD can't hunt that here") end)

    hunt_arm("^(?:Not while you are fighting!|You can't hunt while (?:resting|sitting)\\.|You dream about going on a nice hunting trip)",
        function() hunt_stop("can't hunt right now") end)

    send("hunt " .. mobName)
end

--[[
    The hunt trick.

    During a campaign the MUD refuses to hunt your actual target — "You seem
    unable to hunt that target for some reason." — while every decoy sharing
    the keyword returns an ordinary direction. So the refusal is the signal:
    walk 'hunt 1.guard', 'hunt 2.guard' and so on until one fails, and that
    index is your mob. Then 'where 4.guard' says which room it's in.

    Only useful mid-campaign, and the MUD keeps refusing even after the kill
    until the campaign ends, which is why a hit is reported rather than acted
    on automatically.
]]
local trick = { keyword = nil, alt = nil, n = 0, trig = {}, max = 25 }

local function trick_untrig()
    for _, id in pairs(trick.trig) do removeTrigger(id) end
    trick.trig = {}
end

local function trick_stop(why)
    trick_untrig()
    local was = trick.keyword
    trick.keyword, trick.alt, trick.n = nil, nil, 0

    if was and why then utilprint(TAGR .. "hunt trick: " .. why .. ".") end
end

--[[
    The keyword to hunt on. Usually the last word of the name — 'a fierce
    guard' is 'guard' — but 133 mobs don't follow that, which is what the
    exceptions table carried over from Mudlet is for.

    Split by hand. This used gmatch over "[a-z]+" and came back with 'a' for
    'a member of the white guard' — string.gmatch runs on the JS regex engine
    and returned the first match rather than iterating, so the loop that was
    meant to walk to the last word never moved off the first. 'hunt 1.a' then
    prefix-matched a wounded adventurer in another room and the trick chased
    the wrong mob entirely.

    Skipping connectives as well as articles matters for the same name: the
    last word is 'guard', but 'of' and 'the' sit between it and 'member'.

    Mobs come in two naming shapes and they want opposite halves of the name:

        Russ the Bartender     -> russ      the proper name, not the title
        Queen Luana            -> luana     ditto, title first this time
        an evil jacket         -> evil jacket
        a member of the white guard -> white guard

    For a description, two words beat one: 'guard' matches any of six in a
    barracks and the trick then walks all of them, where 'white guard' lands
    on the one you want. Multi-word keywords are known good — the Mudlet
    exceptions table holds 'worker bee', 'white shark' and 'vegetable pot pie',
    all worked out against the live MUD.

    Capitalisation is the tell for a proper name, which is the only signal the
    name itself carries. Returns a fallback alongside, because both readings
    are guesses: a builder doesn't have to put the adjective — or the title —
    in the mob's keyword list. The caller drops to the fallback when nothing
    answers to the first choice.
]]
local NOT_KEYWORD = { a = true, an = true, the = true, of = true }

local function keyword_for(name)
    -- an exception was worked out against the MUD; it needs no second guess
    local k = keywords[mob_key(name)]
    if str(k) then return k, nil end

    -- case is kept: the capitals are what distinguish Russ from a bartender
    local words, cur = {}, ""

    for i = 1, string.len(name or "") do
        local c = string.sub(name, i, i)
        local l = string.lower(c)

        if l >= "a" and l <= "z" then
            cur = cur .. c
        elseif cur ~= "" then
            table.insert(words, cur)
            cur = ""
        end
    end
    if cur ~= "" then table.insert(words, cur) end

    if #words > 0 and NOT_KEYWORD[string.lower(words[1])] then
        table.remove(words, 1)
    end
    if #words == 0 then return nil, nil end

    -- 'Russ the Bartender' — everything from 'the' on is a title
    if #words >= 3 and string.lower(words[2]) == "the" then
        return string.lower(words[1]), string.lower(words[#words])
    end

    -- any other proper name: the last capitalised word carries it
    for i = #words, 1, -1 do
        local head = string.sub(words[i], 1, 1)
        if head >= "A" and head <= "Z" and not NOT_KEYWORD[string.lower(words[i])] then
            return string.lower(words[i]), nil
        end
    end

    -- plain description: adjective plus noun, with the bare noun in reserve
    local last, at = nil, 0
    for i = #words, 1, -1 do
        if not NOT_KEYWORD[string.lower(words[i])] then
            last = string.lower(words[i])
            at   = i
            break
        end
    end

    if not last then return nil, nil end

    local prev = (at > 1) and string.lower(words[at - 1]) or nil
    if prev and NOT_KEYWORD[prev] then prev = nil end

    if prev then return prev .. " " .. last, last end
    return last, nil
end

local function trick_step()
    if not trick.keyword then return end

    trick.n = trick.n + 1
    if trick.n > trick.max then
        trick_stop("no refusal in " .. trick.max .. " tries — wrong area, or not on a campaign")
        return
    end

    send("hunt " .. trick.n .. "." .. trick.keyword)
end

local function trick_start(name)
    local target = trim(name or "")

    if string.lower(target) == "stop" then
        trick_stop("cancelled")
        return
    end

    -- no argument: the first outstanding campaign target. Never a quest one —
    -- those hunt normally, so there is no refusal to detect
    if target == "" then
        for _, t in ipairs(targets.campaign or {}) do
            if not t.done then target = t.mob break end
        end
    end

    if target == "" then
        for _, t in ipairs(targets.gquest or {}) do
            if not t.done then target = t.mob break end
        end
    end

    if target == "" then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "ht <mob>   (or take a campaign first)")
        return
    end

    local kw, alt = keyword_for(target)
    if not kw then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "no keyword to hunt for '" .. target .. "'.")
        return
    end

    trick_stop()
    trick.keyword, trick.alt, trick.n = kw, alt, 0
    -- names the mob too: a keyword that looks wrong is only diagnosable if
    -- you can see what it was derived from
    utilprint(TAG .. "hunt trick on '" .. kw .. "' (" .. target .. ")...")

    -- the refusal: this index is the campaign target
    table.insert(trick.trig, addTrigger("^You seem unable to hunt that target for some reason\\.$",
        function()
            local hit = trick.n
            local kwd = trick.keyword
            trick_untrig()
            trick.keyword, trick.n = nil, 0

            utilprint(TAG .. "target is $Y" .. hit .. "." .. kwd .. "$w — checking where.")
            send("where " .. hit .. "." .. kwd)
        end, { type = "regex" }))

    -- an ordinary direction means this one is a decoy; try the next
    table.insert(trick.trig, addTrigger("^You are (?:confident|(?:almost )?certain) that .+ (?:passed through here|is)",
        function() trick_step() end, { type = "regex" }))

    -- ran out of mobs with that keyword
    table.insert(trick.trig, addTrigger("^No one in this area by (?:the name '.+'|that name)\\.",
        function()
            --[[
                Nothing answered on the very first index, which means the
                keyword itself is wrong rather than the target being absent —
                the builder didn't give the mob its adjective, or its title.
                Drop to the reserve and start over instead of reporting a miss.
            ]]
            if trick.n <= 1 and str(trick.alt) and trick.alt ~= trick.keyword then
                trick.keyword, trick.alt, trick.n = trick.alt, nil, 0
                utilprint(TAG .. "nothing answers to that — retrying on '" .. trick.keyword .. "'.")
                trick_step()
                return
            end

            trick_stop("ran out at " .. trick.n .. " — none of them refused, so the target isn't here")
        end, { type = "regex" }))

    table.insert(trick.trig, addTrigger("^(?:Not while you are fighting!|You can't hunt while (?:resting|sitting)\\.)",
        function() trick_stop("can't hunt right now") end, { type = "regex" }))

    trick_step()
end

--[[
    'You cannot run to <area>.'

    Not every area is runto-able. The keyword was right — it came from the seed
    database, not a guess — and the MUD still refuses, because runto only
    reaches areas with a path defined for it. Left alone that is a dead end
    with no next step offered, which is the least useful moment to say nothing.

    We usually know more than runto does: if this mob has ever been seen, its
    room id is recorded, and walking there is a click. So the refusal answers
    with what we have rather than restating the failure.
]]
local function on_no_runto(captures, line)
    --[[
        Taken off the line itself rather than out of a capture group: this
        plugin reads its triggers through as_text for exactly that reason, and
        which index a capture lands on is the one thing nobody here has ever
        been sure of.
    ]]
    local text = as_text(captures, line) or ""
    local head = "You cannot run to "

    local area = text
    local at = string.find(text, head, 1, true)
    if at then area = string.sub(text, at + string.len(head)) end

    area = trim(area)
    if string.sub(area, -1) == "." then
        area = string.sub(area, 1, string.len(area) - 1)
    end

    local targ = str(quest.targ) and quest.targ or nil
    if not targ then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "the MUD won't run to " .. area
            .. " - it has no runto path. Walk or portal in.")
        return
    end

    local list = mobs[mob_key(targ)]
    local shown = 0

    if type(list) == "table" then
        for _, r in ipairs(list) do
            local id = tonumber(r.roomid) or 0
            if id > 0 and shown < 3 then
                shown = shown + 1
                hyperlink("$Y" .. (str(r.room) and r.room or ("room " .. id))
                    .. " (" .. id .. ")$w", "/snd go " .. id,
                    { hint = "walk there" })
            end
        end
    end

    if shown == 0 then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "the MUD won't run to " .. area
            .. ", and " .. targ .. " has never been seen. 'mobwhere " .. targ
            .. "' may know.")
    else
        utilprint(TAG .. area .. " has no runto path - but " .. targ
            .. " has been seen here. Click to walk.")
    end
end

--[[
    Aardwolf's own speedwalk, run-length encoded.

        e, w, w, e, s   ->   run e2wes

    The count goes IN FRONT of the direction and a single step carries none.
    One command the MUD walks itself beats fifty sent one at a time, and it
    survives a laggy connection in a way a client-side walker does not.

    nil when any step isn't a compass direction — a portal, a 'climb rope', a
    special exit. 'run' can't express those, and half a route is worse than
    none, so the caller falls back to walking it step by step.
]]
local RUNDIR = {
    n = "n", s = "s", e = "e", w = "w", u = "u", d = "d",
    north = "n", south = "s", east = "e", west = "w", up = "u", down = "d",
}

--[[
    Custom exits win, every time.

    findPath costs a plain compass step and a custom exit the same, so where a
    room has both it takes the compass one — 47195 has 'w: 49260' AND
    'west;;say hi: 49260', and the route came back as a bare 'w'.

    That is backwards for walking. A custom exit exists because someone
    recorded the thing that ACTUALLY works: unlock it, open it, ride it, say
    the word. The compass twin beside it is the move that fails when the door
    is shut. Preferring the cexit costs nothing when they are equivalent and
    saves the walk when they are not.

    The path hands back vnums alongside directions, so each step's destination
    is known and getSpecialExits(room) answers { [command] = destVnum } — the
    substitution is just "is there a command from here that lands in the same
    room".

    Where several reach it, the LONGEST wins. Bootcamp's 49260 carries both
    'get bus bag' and 'get bus bag;;unlock down;;open down;;down;;close up',
    and the long one is the full ritual — the short one is what works only when
    the door already happens to be open. Ties break alphabetically so the same
    route is the same route twice.
]]
local function with_cexits(path, from)
    local dirs = mapl(path.directions)

    if #dirs == 0 or type(getSpecialExits) ~= "function" then return dirs end

    local vnums = mapl(path.vnums)
    local prev  = tonumber(from)

    for i = 1, #dirs do
        local dest = tonumber(vnums[i])

        if prev and dest then
            local okx, sp = pcall(getSpecialExits, prev)

            if okx and type(sp) == "table" then
                -- length carried alongside rather than re-read off `best`,
                -- so nothing here depends on comparing a local to nil
                local best    = nil
                local bestLen = -1

                for key, v in pairs(sp) do
                    if tonumber(v) == dest then
                        local cmd = tostring(key)
                        local len = string.len(cmd)
                        if len > bestLen or (len == bestLen and cmd < tostring(best)) then
                            best, bestLen = cmd, len
                        end
                    end
                end

                if best then dirs[i] = best end
            end
        end

        prev = dest
    end

    return dirs
end

--[[
    A path, as the fewest commands that walk it.

    Compass runs collapse into Aardwolf's own speedwalk; anything that isn't a
    direction — a portal, 'climb rope', any custom exit the mapper holds — is a
    command in its own right, so the run is broken either side of it:

        e w w e s  [enter portal]  n e e e s s
        ->  run e2wes
            enter portal
            run n3e2s

    Which beats the old behaviour of abandoning 'run' the moment a path had one
    odd step in it — a portal in the middle used to cost you the speedwalk for
    the whole route.

    And it beats handing the whole thing to walkTo, which was tried and taken
    back out. The walker single-steps — 'd' 'd' 'd' 'd' 'n' 'n' 'e' 'e', one
    command per room — and it ignores the custom exit we substituted in, so
    gauntlet's 31652 sent a bare 'd' into a closed pile of boulders four times
    and then kept going after the route had already failed. 'run' is one
    command for the whole leg and Aardwolf stops it when it cannot continue.

    Sent as separate commands rather than one ';'-joined line: Aardwolf has no
    client-side separator, so a ';' would go to the MUD as literal text.
]]
local function route(dirs)
    if type(dirs) ~= "table" then return nil end

    local out, walk, prev, n = {}, "", nil, 0

    local function flush_dir()
        if prev then walk = walk .. ((n > 1) and tostring(n) or "") .. prev end
        prev, n = nil, 0
    end

    local function flush_run()
        flush_dir()
        if walk ~= "" then
            table.insert(out, "run " .. walk)
            walk = ""
        end
    end

    for _, raw in ipairs(dirs) do
        local step = trim(tostring(raw))
        local d    = RUNDIR[string.lower(step)]

        if d then
            if d == prev then
                n = n + 1
            else
                flush_dir()
                prev, n = d, 1
            end
        elseif step ~= "" then
            flush_run()

            --[[
                A special exit is a COMMAND, and it may be several.

                    Custom exit saved: 47195 --[west;;say hi]--> 49260

                MudForge joins them with ';;'. Aardwolf has no client-side
                separator of its own, so that has to be split before it goes on
                the wire or the semicolons arrive as literal text.

                Only ';;'. Bootcamp's 49260 carries an exit written with single
                semicolons — 'get bus bag;unlock down;open down;...' — and
                whether the client expands those or treats the lot as one
                command name is not documented either way. Splitting on a
                single ';' on the strength of a guess would break every exit of
                that shape.

                The parts go out as their own commands rather than rejoining a
                'run': 'open down;;down' has to send 'open down' and then 'down'
                in that order, and folding that 'down' into the next run would
                do it before the door was open.
            ]]
            -- wait(N) is a pause the CLIENT takes, not a command. On the
            -- wire it is just a word the MUD does not know, and everything
            -- after it lands before the door has finished opening.
            local function push(cmd)
                cmd = trim(cmd)
                if cmd == "" then return end
                if string.find(string.lower(cmd), "^wait%s*%(") then return end
                table.insert(out, cmd)
            end

            local part, i = "", 1
            while i <= string.len(step) do
                if string.sub(step, i, i + 1) == ";;" then
                    push(part)
                    part, i = "", i + 2
                else
                    part = part .. string.sub(step, i, i)
                    i = i + 1
                end
            end
            push(part)
        end
    end

    flush_run()

    if #out == 0 then return nil end
    return out
end

local function go(roomid, area)
    local id = tonumber(roomid)

    if id and id > 0 and roomExists(id) then
        --[[
            Routed from where you are AT THIS MOMENT, not from wherever the
            panel was drawn. You may have walked half the continent since the
            campaign was listed, and a path worked out then is a path from
            somewhere you no longer are.
        ]]
        --[[
            A room id, or nothing. NOT just "a number".

            getPlayerRoom answers with the Mudlet convention for don't-know,
            which is -1 rather than nil — and -1 is a number, so a plain type()
            check accepted it, skipped the fallback to GMCP, failed the
            from > 0 test, and dropped silently through to walkTo. That is the
            'walking to 16236' with no run behind it.
        ]]
        local function room_id(v)
            v = tonumber(v)
            if v and v > 0 then return v end
            return nil
        end

        local from = nil
        if type(getPlayerRoom) == "function" then
            local okp, v = pcall(getPlayerRoom)
            if okp then from = room_id(v) end
        end
        --[[
            GMCP straight, not through here(): that helper is defined 700 lines
            BELOW this one, so calling it from up here is a nil global and the
            whole click dies. It only ever ran when getPlayerRoom came back
            unknown, which is the one path nobody clicks until it matters.
        ]]
        if not from then
            local r = gmcp_get({ "room.info", "Room.Info" })
            if type(r) == "table" then from = room_id(r.num) end
        end

        if from == id then
            utilprint(TAG .. "you're already there.")
            return
        end

        --[[
            Say what went wrong, out loud.

            Every failure here used to read the same on screen — 'walking to
            <id>' — whether the map wasn't ready, the route didn't exist, or
            the function wasn't there at all. One line that names the reason is
            the difference between a bug report and a guess.
        ]]
        local why = nil

        if not from then
            why = "don't know which room you're in"
        elseif type(findPath) ~= "function" then
            why = "this build has no findPath"
        else
            local ok, path = pcall(findPath, from, id)

            if not ok then
                why = "findPath failed: " .. tostring(path)
            elseif type(path) ~= "table" then
                why = "findPath gave back a " .. type(path)
            elseif not path.found then
                why = "no route from " .. from
                    .. (str(path.error) and (" (" .. path.error .. ")") or "")
            else
                local r = route(with_cexits(path, from))

                if r then
                    utilprint(TAG .. table.concat(r, "$K  ;  $w")
                        .. "   ($C" .. tostring(path.distance or "?") .. " rooms$w)")
                    for _, cmd in ipairs(r) do send(cmd) end
                    return
                end
                why = "the route has no steps this can send"
            end
        end

        --[[
            No route is not the same as nowhere to go. Two rooms can both be on
            the map with nothing joining them — an import that never walked the
            link, a portal-only entrance — and the MUD's own runto crosses that
            without caring what our map thinks.
        ]]
        if str(area) then
            utilprint(TAGR .. why .. " - running to the area instead.")
            if runto(area) then return end
        end

        utilprint(TAGR .. why .. " - letting the client walk to " .. id .. ".")
        walkTo(id)
        return
    end

    if str(area) and runto(area) then return end

    if id and id > 0 then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "room " .. id .. " isn't mapped and no area to run to.")
    else
        utilprint(TAGR .. "nowhere recorded for that one.")
    end
end

local function clear(kind)
    tdirty = true
    targets[kind] = {}
end

--[[
    Ask the MUD to resend the current tab's list.

    Quest goes over GMCP, so 'request quest' brings back a comm.quest status
    packet. Campaign and gquest have no GMCP equivalent and are re-read from
    their normal output, which the triggers pick up as usual.
]]
local function refresh_tab(kind)
    if kind == "quest" then
        sendGMCP("request quest")
        utilprint(TAG .. "asked for quest status.")
    elseif kind == "campaign" then
        send("cp check")
    elseif kind == "gquest" then
        send("gq check")
    end
end

local function add_target(kind, mob, area, need, room)
    tdirty = true

    --[[
        Never the same target twice.

        The burst boundary is a timing guess — two listings issued back to back
        land inside one gap and merge, which is how a 13-target campaign drew
        14 rows with a leftover on top. A campaign never asks for the same mob
        in the same place on two lines (it says 'Find and kill 3 *' instead), so
        a repeat is always the boundary having missed, and dropping it costs
        nothing.
    ]]
    local m, a = trim(mob or ""), trim(area or "")
    for _, t in ipairs(targets[kind] or {}) do
        if t.mob == m and t.area == a then return end
    end

    table.insert(targets[kind], {
        mob  = trim(mob or ""),
        area = trim(area or ""),
        -- the MUD names the ROOM as well as the area on a quest, and dropping
        -- it here is what left GO guessing which 'The Common Room' was meant
        room = trim(room or ""),
        need = tonumber(need) or 1,
        got  = 0,
        done = false,
    })
end

--[[
    Cross off the one that died.

    'Congratulations, that was one of your CAMPAIGN mobs!' doesn't name it, and
    this used to answer that by ticking the first target still outstanding —
    which is right only when you kill them in list order. Kill the third one and
    the panel crossed off the first, so the list stopped matching the campaign
    and stayed wrong for the rest of it.

    The MUD does name it, a line or two earlier: the death line and the corpse
    lines both carry the mob. Whoever last died is passed in here, and the first
    outstanding target that matches it is the one to cross off.

    Falls back to the old guess when nothing matched — a duplicate mob name in
    one campaign, or a death line phrased in a way the triggers don't catch,
    should still tick something rather than leave a killed target sitting there.
]]
--[[
    One kill counts once.

    'Kill at least 3 * a dark knight' is three kills, and this crossed the row
    off on the first one — so a gquest read as finished with two thirds of it
    still alive, and the panel stopped being any help exactly when you still
    needed it.
]]
local function score(t)
    t.got  = (tonumber(t.got) or 0) + 1
    t.done = t.got >= (tonumber(t.need) or 1)
    return t
end

local function tick_off(kind, name)
    tdirty = true

    local want = string.lower(trim(name or ""))

    if want ~= "" then
        -- exact first. 'harpy' and 'a filthy harpy' can both be on one
        -- campaign, and a loose match taken in list order would cross off
        -- whichever came first rather than the one that died.
        for _, t in ipairs(targets[kind] or {}) do
            if not t.done and string.lower(trim(t.mob or "")) == want then
                return score(t)
            end
        end

        --[[
            Then either way round, because neither side is reliably the whole
            name: the target list has 'a dark knight' while the death line can
            be 'A dark knight collapses as the life is hammered out of her. She
            is DEAD!' — the name is in there, with a sentence wrapped round it.
        ]]
        for _, t in ipairs(targets[kind] or {}) do
            local mob = string.lower(trim(t.mob or ""))
            if not t.done and mob ~= "" then
                if string.find(want, mob, 1, true) or string.find(mob, want, 1, true) then
                    return score(t)
                end
            end
        end
    end

    for _, t in ipairs(targets[kind] or {}) do
        if not t.done then return score(t) end
    end
    return nil
end
