local lookup = {}                 -- last mobwhere result, for the panel

--[[
    Numbered, and coloured by whether you can actually get there — the two
    things the MUSHclient list got right. The number is the handle 'snd go
    <n>' uses, and red means the area is one we hold no keyword for, so runto
    is a guess rather than a certainty.
]]
--[[
    The offer, if there is still one to make.

    An invitation that outlives the quest it names is worse than no invitation:
    press JOIN on a global quest that finished twenty minutes ago and the MUD
    just says no. It goes when the quest is won, when you join anything, and
    when it is simply too old — a global quest runs about 81 ticks, so an offer
    older than that is about a quest that cannot still be open.

    Cleared here rather than only read past, so the tab badge and the row agree
    without either having to remember the rule.
]]
local GQ_OFFER_MAX = 45 * 60 * 1000     -- ms; comfortably past a quest's life

local function gq_offer()
    if type(gqOffer) ~= "table" then return nil end
    if gqNum ~= nil then return nil end          -- already in one

    if num(gqOffer.at) and (getCurrentTime() - gqOffer.at) > GQ_OFFER_MAX then
        gqOffer = nil
        return nil
    end

    return gqOffer
end

local function gq_offer_row()
    -- NOT "gqOffer": that is the file-scope one, and shadowing it fails the
    -- whole plugin load. See NOTES 9b.
    local offer = gq_offer()
    if not offer then return "" end

    return '<div class="qready">' .. icon("gquest")
        .. '<b>Global quest #' .. offer.num .. '</b>'
        .. ' · levels ' .. offer.lo .. '–' .. offer.hi
        .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="gqjoin" data-mud-data="' .. offer.num
        .. '" title="gquest join ' .. offer.num .. '">join</span>'
        .. '</div>'
end

--[[
    Both clocks are stored as the moment they run out, not as the minutes the
    MUD said. GMCP only speaks when something changes, so a stored duration is
    a countdown that never counts — and a reconnect leaves stale minutes
    sitting there looking authoritative.
]]
local function left_sec(at)
    if not num(at) then return nil end

    local rest = (at - getCurrentTime()) / 1000
    if rest < 0 then return 0 end
    return rest
end
--[[
    "6 days, 20 hours and 45 minutes" -> seconds.

    Read by looking for each unit rather than by matching the sentence, because
    the sentence changes shape as it shrinks — days drop off, then hours, and
    singular and plural both appear. Anything it does not find is zero.
]]
local function span_secs(text)
    text = string.lower(tostring(text or ""))

    local function unit(word, mult)
        local n = string.match(text, "([0-9]+) " .. word)
        return (tonumber(n) or 0) * mult
    end

    local total = unit("day", 86400) + unit("hour", 3600) + unit("minute", 60)
    if total <= 0 then return nil end
    return total
end
--[[
    The campaign's own clock, the same shape as the quest's.

    A campaign runs for days rather than minutes, so the number that matters is
    days and hours, not seconds — but it is the same idea: how long you have,
    and whether you can take another one.
]]
local function camp_clock()
    local left = left_sec(camp.deadline)
    if left and left > 0 then return left end
    return nil
end
local function long_clock(sec)
    sec = math.max(0, math.floor(tonumber(sec) or 0))

    local d = math.floor(sec / 86400)
    local h = math.floor((sec - d * 86400) / 3600)
    local m = math.floor((sec - d * 86400 - h * 3600) / 60)

    if d > 0 then return d .. "d " .. h .. "h" end
    if h > 0 then return h .. "h " .. m .. "m" end
    return m .. "m"
end

--[[
    The clock line for the tab you are on, in the same place and shape the
    quest tab puts its own. A campaign runs for days and a global quest counts
    in ticks, so neither is a MM:SS — but both answer the same question, which
    is how long you have got.
]]
local function tab_meta(kind)
    if kind == "campaign" then
        local left = camp_clock()
        if left then
            return '<div class="meta">' .. icon("campaign")
                .. 'Campaign ends in <b data-mud-bind="cpclock">'
                .. long_clock(left) .. '</b></div>'
        end
        if camp.needLevel == true then
            return '<div class="meta">' .. icon("campaign")
                .. 'Level before you can take another campaign.</div>'
        end
        return ""
    end

    if kind == "gquest" then
        --[[
            Both numbers, because both are worth having: the tick count is what
            the MUD actually counts and the clock is what you plan around. 81
            ticks at the measured rate is 40:30, and the tick count sitting
            beside it is what stops the clock reading as exact.
        ]]
        local function ticks(n)
            return '<b>' .. n .. '</b> tick' .. ((n == 1) and "" or "s")
                .. ' <span class="zn">(' .. clock(n * tickMs / 1000) .. ')</span>'
        end

        if num(gqStart) then
            return '<div class="meta">' .. icon("gquest")
                .. 'Starts in ' .. ticks(gqStart) .. '</div>'
        end
        if num(gqLeft) then
            return '<div class="meta">' .. icon("gquest")
                .. 'Time left: ' .. ticks(gqLeft) .. '</div>'
        end
    end

    return ""
end

--[[
    The area you are standing in, as the map spells it.

    Worked out ONCE per render. It is the same answer for every row, and the
    reads behind it are a bridge call each.
]]
local function here_area()
    if type(getPlayerRoom) ~= "function" or type(getMapRoom) ~= "function" then return nil end

    local okp, v = pcall(getPlayerRoom)
    if not okp then return nil end

    v = tonumber(v)
    -- -1 is the Mudlet convention for don't-know, and it is a number, so a
    -- plain type() check waves it straight through
    if not v or v <= 0 then return nil end

    local okr, r = pcall(getMapRoom, v)
    if not okr or type(r) ~= "table" then return nil end

    local zone = fld(r, "area") or fld(r, "zone")
    if type(zone) ~= "string" or trim(zone) == "" then return nil end
    return string.lower(trim(zone))
end

local function target_rows(kind)
    local all = targets[kind] or {}

    -- indices are only meaningful against the rows this call is about to draw
    goRows, runRows = {}, {}

    local hereArea = here_area()

    local offer = ((kind == "gquest") and gq_offer_row() or "") .. tab_meta(kind)

    if #all == 0 then
        return offer .. '<div class="empty">No ' .. kind .. ' targets</div>'
    end

    --[[
        Grouped by AREA, and within an area the finished ones sink.

        The list arrives in the order the MUD read it out, which is no order at
        all once you are working through it — the rows still to do end up
        scattered among the ones already done, and two targets in the same area
        can sit six rows apart. You clear an area at a time, so the panel
        should read that way.

        Blank areas go last rather than first: an empty string sorts before
        every letter, which would have put the ones we know least about at the
        top. Stable within a group by original index, so equal rows keep the
        MUD's order instead of shuffling on each repaint.
    ]]
    local list, done = {}, 0
    for i, t in ipairs(all) do
        t.ord = i
        if t.done then done = done + 1 end
        if not (t.done and cfg.hidedone) then table.insert(list, t) end
    end

    table.sort(list, function(a, b)
        local aa = string.lower(trim(a.area or ""))
        local ba = string.lower(trim(b.area or ""))

        if (aa == "") ~= (ba == "") then return ba == "" end
        if aa ~= ba then return aa < ba end

        if (a.done == true) ~= (b.done == true) then return b.done == true end
        return a.ord < b.ord
    end)

    if #list == 0 then
        return '<div class="empty">All ' .. done .. ' ' .. kind
            .. ' target(s) done</div>'
    end

    local out = offer
    for i, t in ipairs(list) do
        --[[
            The area is what the MUD gives; the room comes from our own
            sightings. Offer a walk only when we actually know a room id,
            rather than a button that fails when pressed.
        ]]
        local hits = where(t.mob)
        local dest = (#hits > 0) and hits[1] or nil

        --[[
            Worked out BEFORE the markup that reads them. These were declared
            below their first use, which under the transpiler doesn't raise —
            it hoists and hands you undefined — so every row rendered class
            "t undefined" and an area of "unknown" no matter what the MUD had
            said. Lua would have caught it; JavaScript quietly didn't.
        ]]
        local dest_area = (t.area ~= "" and t.area) or (dest and dest.zone) or ""

        --[[
            When what the MUD gave is a ROOM, the map turns it into the area
            it belongs to and the row gets both: the room the target is in,
            and the area to run to. Rows used to show the room where the area
            goes and then call it unknown.
        ]]
        local mudRoom, runKey, mudVnum = nil, nil, nil
        -- set when mudVnum came from the room the MUD named THIS TICK, rather
        -- than from an area name we had to work backwards out of
        local mudLive = false

        --[[
            Whether the thing in dest_area is an AREA at all.

            False means the MUD named a room, nothing could resolve it, and
            what is on screen is a room name standing in for an area. Which
            makes "are you in it?" unanswerable — see the where button below.
        ]]
        --[[
            An EXACT area name, or something that merely contains one.

            area_key falls back to a substring match either way round, so 'In
            the Lair of the Graveyard Lord' answers 'graveyard' — which is the
            right area, and is also a ROOM name, and the room-to-area block
            below never ran because area_key had already said yes. The row
            printed the same string on both sides of the separator:

                In the Lair of the Graveyard Lord · In the Lair of the Graveyard Lord

            So an inexact hit is treated as what it is: a room name that
            happens to name its area.
        ]]
        local exactArea = (areas[string.lower(trim(dest_area))] ~= nil)
        local looseKey  = area_key(dest_area)
        local areaKnown = (looseKey ~= nil)

        if str(dest_area) and looseKey ~= nil and not exactArea then
            local rec = areaByKey[string.lower(looseKey)]

            mudRoom   = dest_area
            dest_area = (rec and str(rec.name)) or looseKey
            runKey    = looseKey
        end

        --[[
            A key whenever we have one, exact match or not.

            runKey is what the sighting filter below keys off, and it used to
            be set ONLY inside the room-to-area conversion — so an area the MUD
            named outright got no filtering at all, and any sighting anywhere
            could drive GO. That is the walking-out-of-the-area bug again, in
            the one case that looked too simple to have it.

            'the receptionist' is the near miss: six sightings in kerofk
            against a campaign target in newthalos. Same name, different mob,
            different continent.
        ]]
        if runKey == nil and looseKey ~= nil then runKey = looseKey end

        if str(dest_area) and area_key(dest_area) == nil then
            --[[
                Every area we have ever seen this mob in, handed to the room
                lookup so a sighting can outvote a level range.
            ]]
            local seenZones = {}
            for _, h in ipairs(hits) do
                if str(h.zone) then seenZones[string.lower(trim(h.zone))] = true end
            end

            local resolved = area_of_room(dest_area, seenZones)
            if resolved then
                mudRoom   = dest_area
                dest_area = resolved.name
                runKey    = resolved.key
                mudVnum   = resolved.vnum

                -- several areas fitted equally well and one was picked: the
                -- where button stays available rather than trusting it
                areaKnown = not resolved.guess

            elseif dest and str(dest.zone) then
                --[[
                    The map could not place the room, but we have STOOD in it.

                    'Egg incubation room 1' is not an area and the map does not
                    know the name, so the row printed it as both the room and
                    the area — "Egg incubation room 1 · Egg incubation room 1"
                    — while the place we were actually standing in was
                    hatchling, and a 'where' walk had just recorded five rooms
                    there with the zone on every one of them.

                    A sighting knows the zone because GMCP said so at the
                    moment we saw it. That beats a name nothing can resolve.
                ]]
                mudRoom   = dest_area
                dest_area = dest.zone
                runKey    = area_key(dest.zone)
                areaKnown = true
            end
        end

        --[[
            Both halves, straight from the MUD.

            A quest arrives over GMCP carrying data.room AND data.area, and
            only the area was being kept — so the room the quest actually named
            was thrown away and the area above had to be INFERRED back out of a
            room name by level fit. Nothing to infer: it was told to us.

            Runs after the block above on purpose. That one only fires when the
            area field turned out to hold a room name, which is the case where
            there is no separate room to use.
        ]]
        --[[
            IN the area, or there is no GO.

            A GO on a row for somewhere you are not is a button that can only
            ever walk you out of where you are standing — which is what it kept
            doing. RUNTO is the honest button from outside, and once it has put
            you in the area GO appears on the next redraw.

            It is also most of the cost gone: room_in_area scans the map, and
            it now only runs for rows you could actually walk to.
        ]]
        local inArea = false
        if hereArea and str(dest_area) then
            inArea = (string.lower(tostring(area_key(dest_area) or dest_area)) == hereArea)
        end

        if str(t.room) and str(dest_area) then
            mudRoom = t.room

            if inArea then
                local vn = room_in_area(t.room, area_key(dest_area) or dest_area)
                if vn then mudVnum, mudLive = vn, true end
            end
        end

        --[[
            Stay in the area the campaign named.

            'a rabbit' is in a dozen areas, and the sightings database answers
            with wherever we last happened to see one. GO walked to that, so a
            rabbit in The Land of the Beer Goblins sent the character to
            Terramire — the panel naming one area while the button walked to
            another.

            A sighting is only worth using when it is INSIDE the area this
            campaign means. There it is better than the campaign's own room,
            because it is where the mob actually stands rather than the room
            the target list points at. Outside it, it is a different mob in a
            different place and must not be offered at all.
        ]]
        if runKey then
            local inArea = nil
            for _, h in ipairs(hits) do
                if str(h.zone) and string.lower(h.zone) == string.lower(runKey) then
                    inArea = h
                    break
                end
            end
            dest = inArea
        end

        -- prefer a room the mapper actually knows; a sighting in an unmapped
        -- room is still worth showing, but runto is what will get you there
        local mapped = dest and dest.roomid > 0 and roomExists(dest.roomid)

        local known = str(dest_area) and area_key(dest_area) ~= nil

        local state = "unknown"
        if t.done then      state = "done"
        elseif mapped then  state = "mapped"
        elseif known then   state = "known"
        end

        --[[
            Two lines, one card. The name had been sharing a row with four
            buttons and was losing — 'an e…' where the whole point is knowing
            what you're hunting. Name and area get the full width; the buttons
            hang underneath, smaller, indented under the name.
        ]]
        --[[
            The action carries the target's ORIGINAL index, not its position on
            screen. Sorting the finished rows to the bottom means those two
            stopped being the same number, and the handler looks the target up
            in storage order — clicking row 1 would have selected whatever the
            MUD happened to list first, which is the exact bug that made this
            panel cross off the wrong mob once already.

            The number shown is still the position you can see.
        ]]
        out = out .. '<div class="t ' .. state .. '"'
            .. ' data-mud-action="target" data-mud-data="' .. kind .. ':' .. (t.ord or i) .. '">'
            .. '<div class="t1">'
            .. '<span class="num">' .. i .. '</span>'
            .. icon(t.done and "found" or "target")
            .. '<span class="mob">' .. esc(t.mob) .. '</span>'

        --[[
            "2/3", not "x3". The requirement alone says nothing about how far
            through it you are, and that is the only thing you actually want
            from a row you have already started.
        ]]
        if (tonumber(t.need) or 1) > 1 then
            out = out .. '<span class="need">'
                .. (tonumber(t.got) or 0) .. '/' .. t.need .. '</span>'
        end

        --[[
            The AREA always comes from the MUD on the target line itself, so
            it is never a guess. The ROOM is ours, out of the sightings
            database, and that's the half that can be missing — so show the
            area unconditionally and add the room in front of it when we
            happen to know one.
        ]]
        -- escaped per part: esc() on the joined string would turn the
        -- separator's & into & and print a literal "·"
        local place = esc(str(dest_area) or "unknown area")

        -- the MUD's own room wins over one we merely remember seeing it in:
        -- that is where this campaign says the target is, right now
        --[[
            Never the same string on both sides of the separator.

            Whichever branch got us here, a row that reads

                In the Lair of the Graveyard Lord · In the Lair of the Graveyard Lord

            is a room name printed twice because nothing could turn it into an
            area. Saying it once says exactly as much.
        ]]
        local same = function(a, b)
            return string.lower(trim(tostring(a or ""))) == string.lower(trim(tostring(b or "")))
        end

        --[[
            THE NAME IS NOT THE VNUM, and only one of them needs the mapper.

            This was gated on `mapped`, so 'where' could answer "the secretary
            is in Outer Office", print exactly that, and the row beside it went
            on saying nothing but "Kerofk". The room had never been walked, so
            the mapper had no vnum for it, so the name we had been told was
            thrown away with the vnum we did not have.

            Those are two different things. The vnum is what GO needs and GO is
            still gated on it. The NAME is what you need to know where you are
            going, and an unmapped room has one just the same — it is the whole
            answer 'where' exists to give.
        ]]
        if mudRoom and not same(mudRoom, dest_area) then
            place = esc(mudRoom) .. " · " .. place
        elseif dest and str(dest.room) and not same(dest.room, dest_area) then
            place = esc(dest.room) .. " · " .. place
        end

        out = out .. '<span class="area">' .. place .. '</span>'
            .. '</div><div class="t2">'

        --[[
            Four actions, same order every row so they're muscle memory:
            walk there if the map knows it, run to the area otherwise, hunt
            the mob wherever it has wandered to, then kill it.
        ]]
        --[[
            Walk there.

            A campaign target had no GO at all unless we happened to have seen
            that mob before, which for a newbie area nobody has walked is never
            — and quest targets were fine the whole time because GMCP hands
            those over with a real area. But the campaign line names the room,
            and the map turns a room name into a vnum, so there IS somewhere to
            walk to.

            A sighting normally wins — it is where the mob actually was, rather
            than where the campaign says to look. A LIVE room does not lose to
            one: a quest names the room the target is standing in right now
            over GMCP, and a sighting from three days ago is not a better
            answer than that.
        ]]
        local goVnum = nil
        if not inArea then
            -- nothing to offer but the run: see above
        elseif mudLive and type(roomExists) == "function" then
            local okr, exists = pcall(roomExists, mudVnum)
            if okr and exists then goVnum = mudVnum end
        end

        if goVnum or not inArea then
            -- already settled, or not ours to offer
        elseif mapped then
            goVnum = dest.roomid
        elseif mudVnum and type(roomExists) == "function" then
            local okr, exists = pcall(roomExists, mudVnum)
            if okr and exists then goVnum = mudVnum end
        end

        if goVnum then
            -- the area travels with it: with no route between two rooms the
            -- map knows, 'runto' still gets you there, and GO can only offer
            -- that if it was told which area to run to
            table.insert(goRows, { vnum = goVnum, area = runKey or dest_area })

            out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="go" data-mud-data="'
                .. #goRows .. '">go</span>'
        end

        if str(dest_area) then
            --[[
                The KEY when the map gave us one: 'runto jotun' is what Aardwolf
                takes, and it can't be mistaken for another area the way a
                display name can.

                The mob travels with it. Running to the area is half the job —
                the row still has no GO unless something has been seen there,
                and 'where' on arrival is what puts it in the database.
            ]]
            table.insert(runRows, { area = runKey or dest_area, mob = t.mob })

            out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="runto" data-mud-data="'
                .. #runRows .. '">runto</span>'
        end

        --[[
            Standing in the area with nothing to walk to.

            A campaign names the AREA, not the room, so a row only gets a
            walkable vnum once something has been seen there — and in an area
            nobody has walked, nothing ever has. 'where' is what turns that
            into a sighting, and this is the button that says "I am here now,
            go and learn it".

            Only when it would achieve something: in the area, and no GO
            already. Typing 'where' yourself does not feed the database — the
            recorder only listens during a walk this started.
        ]]
        --[[
            In the area — or no idea which area it is.

            The second half breaks a loop. 'Egg incubation room 1' is a room
            the map cannot place, so it stands in for the area, so inArea is
            false, so there is no button — and the button is the thing that
            would have resolved it. You are standing in hatchling looking at a
            target that is right there with no way to say so.

            Asking costs one command and cannot mislead: 'where' only ever
            answers for the area you are in, so it either finds the thing here
            or says there is none.
        ]]
        if (inArea or not areaKnown) and not goVnum then
            out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="where" data-mud-data="'
                .. esc(t.mob) .. '" title="ask the MUD which rooms it is in here, and remember them">where</span>'
        end

        out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="hunt" data-mud-data="'
            .. esc(t.mob) .. '">hunt</span>'

        --[[
            No hunt trick on quests. The trick works because the MUD REFUSES
            to hunt a campaign target, and that refusal is the signal — quest
            mobs hunt normally, so ht would walk all 25 indices finding decoys
            and never get the answer it's looking for. Plain hunt is the right
            tool there, which is the button beside it.
        ]]
        if kind ~= "quest" then
            out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="trick" data-mud-data="'
                .. esc(t.mob) .. '" title="hunt trick: the index the MUD refuses is your target">ht</span>'
        end

        out = out .. '<span class="go kill" data-mud-action="kill" data-mud-data="'
            .. esc(t.mob) .. '">kill</span>'

        out = out .. '</div></div>'
    end

    return out
end




-- days and hours, because "9861:03" is not a campaign deadline anybody reads

local function quest_clock()
    local q = left_sec(quest.deadline)
    if q and q > 0 then return clock(q), "left" end

    local w = left_sec(quest.readyAt)
    if w then
        if w <= 0 then return nil, "ready" end
        return clock(w), "next"
    end

    return nil, nil
end

local function quest_meta()
    if tab ~= "quest" then return "" end

    local bits = {}
    if str(quest.targ) then table.insert(bits, "<b>" .. esc(quest.targ) .. "</b>") end
    if str(quest.room) then table.insert(bits, esc(quest.room)) end

    --[[
        Not twice. When the map cannot place the room, comm.quest hands back
        the same string for both and the header read

            Egg incubation room 1 · Egg incubation room 1

        which says nothing the first half had not already said.
    ]]
    if str(quest.area) and string.lower(trim(quest.area)) ~= string.lower(trim(quest.room or "")) then
        table.insert(bits, esc(quest.area))
    end

    --[[
        One clock at a time — time left on the quest you're on, or the wait
        before the next. Never both: a status reply during the cooldown carries
        a zero timer beside the wait, and showing that read "0:00 left" on a
        panel with 25 real minutes on it.
    ]]
    local qtxt, qstate = quest_clock()

    if qstate == "left" then
        table.insert(bits, '<b data-mud-bind="qclock">' .. qtxt .. '</b> left')
    end

    if quest.turnin ~= true and (qstate == "next" or qstate == "ready") then
        --[[
            Ready, and a button to act on it. "Quest ready" was a statement
            with nothing to press — the quest you just finished offers COMPLETE
            right there, and then the moment the cooldown ends you are back to
            typing it out.
        ]]
        if qstate == "ready" then
            return '<div class="qready">' .. icon("quest") .. '<b>Quest ready</b>'
                .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="qrequest" data-mud-data="1"'
                .. ' title="ask the questmaster for one">request quest</span>'
                .. '</div>'
        end

        -- data-mud-bind lets the clock be pushed in place, so a ticking
        -- countdown doesn't rebuild the panel once a second
        return '<div class="meta">' .. icon("quest")
            .. 'Next quest in <b data-mud-bind="qclock">' .. qtxt .. '</b></div>'
    end

    if #bits == 0 and quest.turnin ~= true then return "" end

    local out = ""
    if quest.turnin == true then
        out = out .. '<div class="turnin">' .. icon("found")
            .. 'Slain — return to the questmaster before the timer runs out'
            .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="qcomplete" data-mud-data="1">quest complete</span>'
            .. '</div>'
    end

    if #bits > 0 then
        out = out .. '<div class="meta">' .. icon("quest")
            .. table.concat(bits, " · ") .. '</div>'
    end

    return out
end

local function mob_rows()
    if #lookup == 0 then
        return '<div class="empty">Nothing looked up yet — try <b>mobwhere <name></b></div>'
    end

    local out = ""
    for i, h in ipairs(lookup) do
        if i > 60 then break end

        out = out .. '<div class="hit">'
            .. '<span class="rm">' .. esc(h.mob) .. ' — ' .. esc(h.room) .. '</span>'
            .. '<span class="zn">' .. esc(h.zone) .. '</span>'
            .. '<span class="ct">' .. h.seen .. 'x</span>'

        if (tonumber(h.roomid) or 0) > 0 and roomExists(h.roomid) then
            out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="go" data-mud-data="' .. h.roomid .. '">go</span>'
        elseif str(h.zone) then
            out = out .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="runto" data-mud-data="'
                .. esc(h.zone) .. '">runto</span>'
        end

        out = out .. '</div>'
    end

    return out
end

render = function()
    --[[
        Every change to a target list ends up here, so this is where the write
        happens — one save per batch rather than six while 'cp check' scrolls
        past. Cheap: a handful of rows, not the mob database.
    ]]
    if tdirty then
        tdirty = false
        pcall(save_targets)
    end

    if not widget then return end

    --[[
        The quest tab says whether you can quest, from wherever you are.

        The countdown lived inside the quest tab, so on the campaign tab there
        was nothing to tell you a quest was 27 minutes away — or that one had
        come up. The tab bar is on screen whichever tab is open, so the state
        belongs there: the wait in place of the count while it runs, and the
        tab lit when it is over.
    ]]
    local qtxt, qstate = quest_clock()

    local bar = ''
    for _, t in ipairs({ "quest", "campaign", "gquest" }) do
        local n     = #(targets[t] or {})
        local extra = ""

        --[[
            The badge is the small text inside a tab, after its name — the
            number in CAMPAIGN 14, the 'READY' in QUEST READY, the clock in
            QUEST 28:58.

            For campaign and gquest that number is MOBS still to kill, not rows
            still listed. Ten rows can be fourteen kills when some of them want
            two, and fourteen is the number you are actually counting down.
        ]]
        local badge = ""

        if t == "campaign" or t == "gquest" then
            local togo = 0
            for _, tg in ipairs(targets[t] or {}) do
                if not tg.done then
                    togo = togo + math.max(0, (tonumber(tg.need) or 1)
                                            - (tonumber(tg.got) or 0))
                end
            end
            if togo > 0 then badge = '<span class="n">' .. togo .. '</span>' end
        end

        if t == "quest" and quest.turnin ~= true then
            if qstate == "next" then
                extra = " cd"
                badge = '<span class="n" data-mud-bind="qtab">' .. qtxt .. '</span>'
            elseif qstate == "ready" then
                extra = " rdy"
                badge = '<span class="n">ready</span>'
            end

        --[[
            A global quest declared for your level is the same kind of moment
            as a quest coming off cooldown: something you can act on right now
            and will otherwise scroll past. Same green, same badge.
        ]]
        elseif t == "gquest" and gq_offer() ~= nil then
            -- colour only: the JOIN button is right there in the panel
            extra = " rdy"

        --[[
            No tick count on the tab. A badge has room for one number and on
            this tab that number is how many targets are left — the clock lives
            in the panel, where it can afford to say "81 ticks (40:30)" and be
            understood.
        ]]
        --[[
            The QUEST countdown is the only clock that belongs on a tab.

            A badge has room for one number, and on every other tab that number
            is how many targets are left. Quest is the exception because it has
            no targets until you have one — the countdown IS its state. The
            campaign and global quest clocks live in the panel, where they can
            afford to say "6d 20h" or "81 ticks (40:30)" and be understood.
        ]]
        elseif t == "campaign" and n == 0 and camp.needLevel == true then
            -- greyed, with the reason in the panel rather than crammed in here
            extra = " cd"
        end

        bar = bar .. '<div class="tb' .. (view == "targets" and tab == t and ' on' or '') .. extra .. '"'
            .. ' data-mud-action="tab" data-mud-data="' .. t .. '">'
            .. icon(t) .. string.upper(t) .. badge .. '</div>'
    end

    --[[
        No MOBS tab. It wrapped the bar onto a second row for something that
        is reached by clicking a target or typing mobwhere, and the row count
        was never the point.
    ]]
    bar = bar .. '<div class="spacer"></div>'

    if view == "mobs" then
        bar = bar .. '<div class="tb on" data-mud-action="view" data-mud-data="targets">'
            .. '◀ targets</div>'
    else
        bar = bar .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="refresh" data-mud-data="' .. tab .. '"'
            .. ' title="ask the MUD to resend this list">↻</div>'
    end

    local body
    if view == "mobs" then
        body = mob_rows()
    else
        body = quest_meta() .. target_rows(tab)
    end

    setWidgetProperty(widget, "content", CSS
        .. '<div class="arc-snd">'
        .. '<div class="bar">' .. bar .. '</div>'
        .. '<div class="body">' .. body .. '</div>'
        .. '</div>')
end

local function here()
    local r = gmcp_get({ "room.info", "Room.Info" })
    if type(r) ~= "table" then return nil, 0, nil end
    return str(r.name), tonumber(r.num) or 0, str(r.zone)
end

local function on_scan(a, b)
    if not cfg.scan then return end

    local name = as_text(a, b)
    if not name then return end

    local room, id, zone = here()
    if id and id > 0 then see(name, room, id, zone, false) end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 'where', which is how the database learns an area it has never walked
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    Walk the indices until the MUD says there is no such thing.

        > where tree
        a tree-climbing boy            The Northern Path
        > where 2.tree
        a tree-climbing boy            The Southern Path
        > where 3.tree
        There is no 3.tree around here.

    The point is NOT to find one room to walk to — findPath already does that
    once something is in the database. The point is that nothing is in the
    database for an area nobody has walked, so a campaign in a newbie zone had
    no GO on any row and no way to get one. 'where' answers for the CURRENT
    AREA ONLY, which makes every hit a sighting we can trust the area of.

    It cannot see what you cannot see, so a hidden mob simply is not there.
]]
local WHERE_MAX = 12        -- a mob in more rooms than this is not a target

--[[
    kw is what goes on the wire, mob is what we show.

    'where a surge of lava' answers "There is no a surge of lava around here."
    for every index — Aardwolf's commands take KEYWORDS and the leading article
    is not one, which huntable() has known all along and this was not calling.

    The walk PACES ITSELF rather than being driven by the replies.

    It used to ask for the next index from inside the hit handler, which meant
    a pattern loose enough for any mob name beside any room name was also the
    thing deciding how many commands to send. Anything else on screen with a
    column of spaces in it counted as a sighting AND drove another index, so a
    mob that was not there reported "learned 3 room(s)" and left 2., 3., 4.
    still going out.

    Now: a timer asks for the next one, the "no such thing" reply ends it, and
    a hit only ever records. A phantom line can no longer make this send
    anything.
]]
--[[
    'where' takes ONE KEYWORD, and we do not know which word it is.

        > where a ball of fur      There is no a ball of fur around here.
        > where ball of fur        There is no ball of fur around here.
        > where ball               a ball of fur      The Main Laboratory

    Stripping the article is not enough — the whole phrase fails too. Aardwolf
    matches a single keyword off the mob, and which word that is is not
    something the name tells you: 'ball' works here, 'warg' is the one for 'an
    escaped helmet-headed warg', and for 'Lyonnair, the wood elf elder' it is
    the first word.

    So the words are tried in order and the MUD decides. A refusal on the FIRST
    index means the keyword was wrong, not that the mob is absent, which is the
    difference between a failed guess and an answer.
]]
local SKIPWORD = {
    ["a"] = true, ["an"] = true, ["the"] = true, ["of"] = true,
    ["in"] = true, ["on"] = true, ["at"] = true, ["from"] = true,
    ["with"] = true, ["and"] = true, ["to"] = true,
}

local function keywords_of(name)
    local out  = {}
    local word = ""
    local text = tostring(name or "") .. " "

    for i = 1, string.len(text) do
        local ch = string.sub(text, i, i)

        if ch == " " then
            -- punctuation is not part of a keyword: 'Lyonnair,' is 'lyonnair'
            local clean = ""
            for j = 1, string.len(word) do
                local c = string.sub(word, j, j)
                if c ~= "," and c ~= "." and c ~= "!" and c ~= "'"
                   and c ~= '"' and c ~= "(" and c ~= ")" then
                    clean = clean .. c
                end
            end

            clean = string.lower(clean)
            if string.len(clean) > 1 and not SKIPWORD[clean] then
                table.insert(out, clean)
            end
            word = ""
        else
            word = word .. ch
        end
    end

    return out
end

--[[
    The keyword that actually worked, per mob.

    'kill' takes one keyword the same way 'where' does, and it CANNOT cycle —
    a wrong guess on 'where' costs a line of output, a wrong guess on 'kill'
    swings at whatever else answers to that word. So it gets the best single
    answer available: the word a 'where' walk already proved, and failing that
    the last word of the name, which is the noun nearly every time ('a ball of
    fur' -> fur, 'an escaped helmet-headed warg' -> warg, 'a swarm of roses'
    -> roses).

    World-scoped rather than in the plugin's own file: those are wiped by the
    remove-and-re-add that installs an update, and this is worth keeping.
]]
local mobkw = {}

local function kw_load()
    local raw = tostring(getVariable("aw_snd_kw") or "")
    local pair, out = "", {}

    for i = 1, string.len(raw) + 1 do
        local ch = (i <= string.len(raw)) and string.sub(raw, i, i) or ";"
        if ch == ";" then
            local cut = string.find(pair, "=", 1, true)
            if cut then
                local k = string.sub(pair, 1, cut - 1)
                local v = string.sub(pair, cut + 1)
                if k ~= "" and v ~= "" then out[k] = v end
            end
            pair = ""
        else
            pair = pair .. ch
        end
    end

    mobkw = out
end

local function kw_save()
    local bits = {}
    for k, v in pairs(mobkw) do table.insert(bits, k .. "=" .. v) end
    setVariable("aw_snd_kw", table.concat(bits, ";"))
end

--[[
    The single keyword to aim a command at this mob with.

    'kill a ball of fur' and 'kill ball of fur' both miss; 'kill ball' does
    not. Proven word if a 'where' walk found one, otherwise the last word of
    the name.
]]
local function kw_for(name)
    local hit = mobkw[mob_key(name)]
    if hit and hit ~= "" then return hit end

    local words = keywords_of(name)
    if #words > 0 then return words[#words] end

    return string.lower(huntable(name))
end

local wh = { mob = "", kw = "", words = {}, wi = 1,
             n = 0, live = false, found = 0, timer = nil, hit = "" }

--[[
    Is this where-line's LEFT column the target we asked about?

    'where intern' answers with every intern in the area, and the campaign
    wanted one of them by its full name:

        a surgical intern              Operating Room
        a surgical intern              Experimental Surgery
        an intern on rounds            A Busy Hallway

    The left column is the mob's full name and the campaign line gives us the
    same string, so this is a comparison rather than a guess. Case-folded and
    with the leading article off both sides, because "A surgical intern" in a
    room description and "a surgical intern" on a target list are the same mob
    and Aardwolf is not consistent about which it prints.
]]
local function where_is_target(found, want)
    local a = string.lower(trim(huntable(found)))
    local b = string.lower(trim(huntable(want)))
    return a ~= "" and a == b
end

local function where_stop()
    wh.live = false
    if wh.timer then clearTimeout(wh.timer) end
    wh.timer = nil
end

local function where_done()
    if not wh.live then return end
    where_stop()

    --[[
        The room the TARGET is in, when one of the lines named it, rather than
        a count of everything the keyword turned up. That count was never the
        answer to the question being asked — "where is the mob I have to kill"
        — and 'learned 13 room(s)' beside a panel still showing no room is a
        report of work done and nothing else.
    ]]
    if wh.hit ~= "" then
        utilprint(TAG .. "$C" .. wh.mob .. "$w is in $C" .. wh.hit .. "$w.")
        save_db()
        render()
    elseif wh.found > 0 then
        utilprint(TAG .. "learned $C" .. wh.found .. "$w room(s) here, but no "
            .. wh.mob .. " among them.")
        save_db()
        render()
    else
        utilprint(TAGR .. "no " .. wh.mob .. " here that you can see.")
    end
end

local function where_next()
    if not wh.live then return end

    wh.n = wh.n + 1
    if wh.n > WHERE_MAX then where_done() return end

    send("where " .. ((wh.n == 1) and wh.kw or (wh.n .. "." .. wh.kw)))

    --[[
        Paced, not chained. The MUD answers in order, so the "there is no N of
        those" for an early index arrives and ends the walk before the later
        ones have been asked for.

        The longer guard is still the backstop for a reply that never comes at
        all — without it this would sit live forever, and every two-column line
        on screen would go into the database as a sighting.
    ]]
    if wh.timer then clearTimeout(wh.timer) end
    wh.timer = setTimeout(function() where_next() end, 600)
end

local function where_start(name)
    local mobName = trim(name or "")
    if mobName == "" then return end

    where_stop()

    local raw = keywords_of(mobName)
    if #raw == 0 then raw = { string.lower(huntable(mobName)) } end

    --[[
        Best guess first, so the usual case costs one command.

        The word a previous walk proved, then the LAST word — the noun, and
        the keyword nearly every time — then everything else in order.
    ]]
    local words, seen = {}, {}
    local proven = mobkw[mob_key(mobName)]

    if proven then table.insert(words, proven); seen[proven] = true end

    local tail = raw[#raw]
    if tail and not seen[tail] then table.insert(words, tail); seen[tail] = true end

    for _, w in ipairs(raw) do
        if not seen[w] then table.insert(words, w); seen[w] = true end
    end

    wh = { mob = mobName, kw = words[1], words = words, wi = 1,
           n = 0, live = true, found = 0, timer = nil, hit = "" }

    utilprint(TAG .. "where " .. mobName .. " $K(learning this area)$w")
    where_next()
end

--[[
    'Alex, the Taskmaster           The Common Room' — mob, then room, run
    together with nothing but a column of spaces between them.

    Two or more spaces is the separator, and the pattern only ever does
    anything while a walk of ours is live. It has to be that loose: a mob name
    can hold anything, and so can a room name.
]]
local function on_where_hit(c, w, line)
    if not wh.live then return end

    local mobName = trim(cap3(c, w, 1, line))
    local room    = trim(cap3(c, w, 2, line))
    if mobName == "" or room == "" then return end

    --[[
        Brackets mean it is not a where hit.

        The prompt, the status line and every tagged channel carry [ ] and can
        easily hold a run of spaces; a mob name and a room name do not. Cheap,
        and it is the difference between learning an area and filling the
        database with fragments of the prompt.
    ]]
    if string.find(mobName .. room, "[", 1, true) then return end
    if string.find(mobName .. room, "]", 1, true) then return end

    --[[
        The area comes from where WE are standing, not from the room name.
        'where' only answers for this area, so that is not an assumption — it
        is the one thing about the reply we know for certain, and it is what
        makes the vnum lookup safe.
    ]]
    local zone = here_area()
    local vnum = 0

    if zone then
        vnum = tonumber(room_in_area(room, zone)) or 0
    end

    -- roomid 0 is "we know the name but not which room": see() handles that,
    -- and a later sighting with a real vnum replaces it
    see(mobName, room, vnum, zone or "", false)
    wh.found = wh.found + 1

    -- the keyword the MUD just answered to, for kill and hunt to use
    if wh.kw ~= "" then
        mobkw[mob_key(wh.mob)] = wh.kw
        mobkw[mob_key(mobName)] = wh.kw
        kw_save()
    end

    --[[
        THE LEFT COLUMN IS THE ANSWER. STOP.

        'where intern' in the hospital walked 1. through 6. and collected
        thirteen rooms, when the second line it read already said "a surgical
        intern — Operating Room" and that was the whole question. Four of the
        remaining commands were answered "There is no 4.intern around here",
        which is six round trips spent to learn nothing.

        The other lines are still worth having — a keyword that turns up three
        mobs has told us about three mobs, and that is how an area gets learned
        — so they go into the database on the way past. What they do not do is
        keep the walk going once the target itself has been found.
    ]]
    if wh.hit == "" and where_is_target(mobName, wh.mob) then
        wh.hit = room
        where_done()
    end
end

local function on_where_none()
    if not wh.live then return end

    --[[
        Refused on the FIRST index with nothing found: that is the keyword
        being wrong, not the mob being absent. Try the next word.

        Only on the first — a refusal at 2. or later is the MUD saying there
        are no more of them, which is the walk finishing normally.
    ]]
    if wh.n <= 1 and wh.found == 0 and wh.wi < #wh.words then
        wh.wi = wh.wi + 1
        wh.kw = wh.words[wh.wi]
        wh.n  = 0
        where_next()
        return
    end

    where_done()
end

--[[
    Run to the area, then ask where the thing is.

    Two steps, because runto TRAVELS — it is a walk across the world, not a
    call that returns. 'where' sent now would answer for wherever we happen to
    be standing at this instant, which is not the area we are heading for, and
    'where' only ever answers for the area you are in.

    So it is armed and the arrival fires it. Already there, and there is
    nothing to wait for.
]]
local pend = { mob = nil, area = nil, at = 0 }

local function run_and_where(area, mob)
    local mobName = trim(mob or "")
    local key     = string.lower(trim(tostring(area or "")))

    if mobName ~= "" and here_area() == key then
        where_start(mobName)
        return
    end

    if mobName ~= "" then
        pend.mob, pend.area, pend.at = mobName, key, getCurrentTime()
    end

    runto(area)
end

--[[
    Armed by run_and_where and fired by the arrival, once.

    The expiry matters: a runto that never lands — refused, interrupted, walked
    off by hand — would otherwise leave this armed, and the next time you
    wandered into that area at any point in the session it would fire a 'where'
    you never asked for.
]]
local function where_on_arrival(zone)
    if pend.mob == nil then return end

    if (getCurrentTime() - pend.at) > 180000 then
        pend.mob, pend.area = nil, nil
        return
    end

    if pend.area ~= nil and pend.area ~= zone then return end

    local mobName = pend.mob
    pend.mob, pend.area = nil, nil
    where_start(mobName)
end

local function on_damage(a, b)
    local name = as_text(a, b)
    if not name then return end

    local room, id, zone = here()
    if id and id > 0 then see(name, room, id, zone, false) end
end

--[[
    Rebuild the quest tab from the GMCP store rather than waiting for the next
    packet. comm.quest is event-shaped, so a plugin reloaded mid-quest has no
    state until something happens — which is why the tab can read empty while
    'quest info' plainly shows a target.
]]
--[[
    The clock fields, in the order they have to be read.

    'wait' outranks everything, whatever the action says. A status reply during
    the cooldown carries a zero timer right beside it, so reading the timer
    first is what put "0:00 left" on the panel while score plainly said 25
    minutes. It's in minutes — the stock client multiplies it by 60.

    'timer' carries no such authority; the stock client's branch for it is an
    empty comment. Quests are granted in the 30-60 minute range and the cap is
    well under two hours, so a value past 180 can't be minutes and has to be
    seconds. Both readings are safe inside the range the MUD actually uses.
]]
local function read_clocks(q)
    local wait = num(q.wait)

    if wait ~= nil then
        quest.readyAt = getCurrentTime() + (wait * 60000)
        quest.rang = nil
    elseif str(q.status) == "ready" then
        quest.readyAt = getCurrentTime()
    end

    local t = num(q.timer)
    if t ~= nil and t > 0 then
        local secs = (t > 180) and t or (t * 60)
        quest.deadline = getCurrentTime() + (secs * 1000)
    end
end

local function on_quest(data)
    if type(data) ~= "table" then return end

    tdirty = true

    local action = str(data.action)
    if not action then return end

    if action == "start" or action == "status" then
        --[[
            'status' answers 'request quest' whether or not you're on one, so
            the target is what decides, not the action. Between quests it comes
            back with no target at all.
        ]]
        local targ = str(data.targ)

        if targ and targ ~= "missing" then
            quest.turnin = false
            quest.targ = targ
            quest.room = str(data.room)
            quest.area = str(data.area)

            -- you're on one, so there is no next one pending. Leaving a stale
            -- readyAt here is what had the panel saying "Quest ready" while a
            -- quest was still running.
            quest.readyAt, quest.rang = nil, nil

            clear("quest")
            add_target("quest", targ, quest.area or "", 1, quest.room)

        elseif action == "status" and quest.turnin ~= true then
            --[[
                No target and nothing owed — genuinely between quests.

                The turnin guard matters: once the mob is dead the status reply
                stops naming a target, and clearing on that wiped the "go turn
                it in" reminder at exactly the moment it was the only thing on
                screen worth reading.
            ]]
            clear("quest")
            quest = { readyAt = quest.readyAt, rang = quest.rang }
        end

        read_clocks(data)

    elseif action == "killed" then
        --[[
            The target is dead but the quest is not over: Aardwolf wants you
            back at the questmaster. Clearing here loses the target's name
            and area right when you still need to know where you were.
            Campaigns don't need this — they complete themselves on the kill.
        ]]
        quest.turnin = true

        for _, t in ipairs(targets.quest or {}) do t.done = true end

    elseif action == "comp" or action == "timeout" or action == "fail" then
        --[[
            All three carry 'wait' — the minutes before another quest can be
            taken. That's the only thing worth showing once the target is
            gone, so keep it rather than resetting to an empty panel.
        ]]
        clear("quest")
        quest = {}
        read_clocks(data)

    elseif action == "ready" then
        quest.readyAt = getCurrentTime()
        quest.rang = nil
    end

    render()
end

local trig = {}

local function arm()
    --[[
        Patterns are lifted from the Mudlet build where they're proven against
        live output. They stay verbatim: retyping a working regex is how you
        introduce a bug that only shows up mid-campaign.
    ]]
    --[[
        Open a campaign listing: clear once, then hold the burst open on a gap.

        Shared by the header and the first target line, because only 'cp info'
        has a header — and because a header that opened the burst without also
        arming the gap left it open until the next target line happened along,
        which could be a different command entirely.
    ]]
    local function begin_cp()
        if not cpFresh then
            clear("campaign")
            cpFresh = true
        end

        if cpTmr then pcall(removeTimer, cpTmr) end
        cpTmr = setTimeout(function() cpFresh, cpTmr = false, nil end, 1200)
    end

    --[[
        The map loads shortly AFTER this plugin does, and until it is warm every
        room lookup answers "don't know". Rows drawn in that window would keep
        the room-as-area reading for as long as the panel sat untouched, so
        redraw once when it comes up.
    ]]
    if type(onMapReady) == "function" then
        pcall(onMapReady, function() render() end)
    end

    trig.cpHeader = addTrigger("^The targets for this campaign are:$",
        begin_cp, { type = "regex" })

    -- runto refusing an area is a dead end unless something offers the next
    -- step; see on_no_runto
    trig.noRunto = addTrigger("^You cannot run to .+\\.$", on_no_runto, { type = "regex" })

    -- and when it offers a choice instead, make the choice clickable
    trig.runtoPick = addTrigger("^\\S+\\s+- \\S.*$", on_runto_choice, { type = "regex" })

    trig.cpTarget = addTrigger("^(?:You still have to kill|Find and kill \\d+) \\* (.+) \\((.+)\\)\\s*$",
        function(a, b)
            local line = as_text(a, b)
            if not line then return end

            --[[
                The burst closes on a gap, not on a footer, because 'cp check'
                hasn't got one. A listing arrives in a single packet, so
                anything still coming a second later is a new command.
            ]]
            begin_cp()

            local mob  = string.match(line, "\\* (.+) \\(")
            local area = string.match(line, "\\(([^)]+)\\)\\s*$")
            if mob then add_target("campaign", mob, area or "", 1) end
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        How long the campaign has, from either command that says so:

            You have 6 days, 20 hours and 45 minutes left to finish this campaign.
            Time Left  ........: [ 6 days, 20 hours and 45 minutes ]

        Stored as a deadline rather than a duration, so it keeps counting down
        between reads instead of freezing at whatever the last one said.
    ]]
    local function set_camp_left(text)
        local secs = span_secs(text)
        if not secs then return end

        camp.deadline = getCurrentTime() + (secs * 1000)
        tdirty = true
        render()
    end

    --[[
        The WHOLE LINE, not a capture.

        span_secs scans for "N days/hours/minutes" wherever they sit, so it
        never needed one — and reaching for capture 1 here meant getting the
        argument order right, which these two did not: every other handler in
        this file is function(a, w, b), and these were function(a, b, w)
        calling cap3(a, w, 1, b). The panel read "Campaign ends in 0m" against
        "You have 6 days, 2 hours and 11 minutes left".

        Nothing else on either line has a number followed by a time unit, so
        scanning the lot is not looser, just harder to get wrong.
    ]]
    trig.cpLeft = addTrigger("^You have .+ left to finish this campaign\\.$",
        function(a, w, b) set_camp_left(as_text(a, b)) end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.cpLeft2 = addTrigger("^Time Left\\s*\\.*:\\s*\\[\\s*.+?\\s*\\]",
        function(a, w, b) set_camp_left(as_text(a, b)) end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        Not a cooldown in minutes like a quest's — you simply cannot take
        another until you level. Worth saying on the tab, because otherwise an
        empty campaign list looks like one you could go and fill.
    ]]
    trig.cpLevel = addTrigger(
        "^You will have to level before you can go on another campaign\\.$",
        function()
            camp.needLevel = true
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.cpNone = addTrigger("^You are not currently on a campaign\\.$", function()
        clear("campaign")
        camp = {}
        cpFresh = false
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.cpDone = addTrigger("^(?:Campaign cleared\\.|CONGRATULATIONS! You have completed your campaign\\.|You may now take another campaign\\.)$",
        function()
            clear("campaign")
            camp = {}
            cpFresh = false
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        A fresh 'gq check' replaces the list; it does not add to it.

        Campaign got this months ago and gquest never did, so every check
        appended: finished targets from the last global quest stayed on the
        panel, and the list only ever grew. Same burst boundary, same reason —
        the lines arrive together, anything a beat later is a new command.
    ]]
    local function begin_gq()
        if not gqFresh then
            clear("gquest")
            gqFresh = true
        end
        if gqTmr then pcall(clearTimeout, gqTmr) end
        gqTmr = setTimeout(function() gqFresh, gqTmr = false, nil end, 1200)
    end

    --[[
        The pattern already captured all three. Re-matching the line with
        string.match repeated the work and, worse, did it with JS regex syntax
        — `\\d` inside a Lua pattern only means anything because these run on a
        JavaScript engine. That makes the parse impossible to exercise anywhere
        but the live client, which is how this went so long without a test.

        Read the captures the trigger handed over.
    ]]
    --[[
        The MUD saying you are not on one. Campaign has had this since the
        start; gquest kept showing the last global quest's targets until the
        next check happened to replace them.

            You are not in a global quest.
            You may win 2 more gquests at this level.
    ]]
    --[[
        A global quest was just declared, and whether it is any use to you is
        entirely a question of your level:

            Global Quest: Global quest # 2393 has been declared for levels
            5 to 16 - less than 25 wins only.

        Kept only when you are inside the range, so the button that appears is
        never one the MUD would refuse. Note the lower-case "quest" here — the
        WIN announcement capitalises it, and matching one pattern against both
        would have been a quiet miss.
    ]]
    trig.gqDecl = addTrigger(
        "^Global Quest: Global quest # (\\d+) has been declared for levels (\\d+) to (\\d+)",
        function(a, b, w)
            local qn = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            local lo = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 2, b)))
            local hi = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 3, b)))
            if not (qn and lo and hi) then return end

            local mine = my_level()
            if mine and (mine < lo or mine > hi) then return end

            gqOffer = { num = qn, lo = lo, hi = hi, at = getCurrentTime() }
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        Joining is where the number is learnt from, and it is the one line that
        says it without ambiguity:

            You have now joined Global Quest # 2393.
    ]]
    trig.gqJoin = addTrigger("^You have now joined Global Quest # (\\d+)",
        function(a, b, w)
            gqNum   = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            gqOffer = nil
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        A global quest that never happened:

            Global Quest: Global quest # 2566 has been cancelled due to lack
            of participants.

        Anchored on "has been cancelled" rather than the reason, because the
        reason is the part likely to vary and is not what this needs to know.
        Lower-case "quest", like the declaration and unlike the win.

        Clears the OFFER if it was for that quest — a JOIN button on a
        cancelled quest is a button that cannot work — and clears the list too
        if it was the one we were in.
    ]]
    trig.gqCancel = addTrigger(
        "^Global Quest: Global quest # (\\d+) has been cancelled",
        function(a, b, w)
            local qn = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            if not qn then return end

            if type(gqOffer) == "table" and gqOffer.num == qn then
                gqOffer = nil
            end

            if gqNum == qn then
                gqNum, gqLeft, gqStart = nil, nil, nil
                clear("gquest")
                gqFresh = false
            end

            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.gqNone = addTrigger("^You are not in a global quest\\.$", function()
        gqNum, gqLeft, gqStart = nil, nil, nil
        clear("gquest")
        gqFresh = false
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        A global quest was won. Verbatim from a live win:

            CONGRATULATIONS!
            You were the first to complete this quest!
            Reward of 28 quest points added.
            Global Quest: Global Quest # 2393 has been won by Solao - 1st win.

        SEVERAL GLOBAL QUESTS RUN AT ONCE, told apart by that number, and this
        announcement goes out for every one of them. The first version matched
        any win and cleared — so somebody else finishing quest #2400 would have
        wiped a list for the #2393 you were still working on.

        Matching the WINNER against your own name is correct as far as it goes:
        if you won, yours is over. It does not yet catch somebody else winning
        the quest YOU are in, which needs the number of the quest you joined,
        and nothing here reads that yet. Until it does, that case falls to
        'You are not in a global quest.' and the next check.

        No name from GMCP means no clear. Guessing wrong here costs the target
        list.
    ]]
    trig.gqWon = addTrigger("^Global Quest: Global Quest # (\\d+) has been won by (\\w+)",
        function(a, b, w)
            -- not "num": there is a file-scope num() and shadowing it fails
            -- the whole plugin load. See NOTES 9b.
            local qnum = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            local who  = string.lower(trim(cap3(a, w, 2, b)))
            local me  = my_name()

            --[[
                Ours if the NUMBER matches the quest we are in — which is the
                case that matters, because somebody else winning it ends it for
                you too. 'gq info' is where that number comes from, so a
                session that has only ever run 'gq check' falls back to "did I
                win it", and a session with neither clears nothing.
            ]]
            --[[
                A win also retires an OFFER for that same quest, whether or not
                it was ours. Leaving it up would put a JOIN button on a global
                quest that is already over.
            ]]
            if type(gqOffer) == "table" and gqOffer.num == qnum then
                gqOffer = nil
                render()
            end

            local mine = (gqNum ~= nil and qnum == gqNum)
                      or (me ~= nil and who == me)
            if not mine then return end

            gqNum, gqLeft, gqStart = nil, nil, nil
            clear("gquest")
            gqFresh = false
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        'gq check' and 'gq info' say the same thing in different words:

            You still have to kill 1 * a pot belly pig (On a busy walkway)
            Kill at least 1 * a pot belly pig (On a busy walkway).

        Only the second was ever matched, so 'gq check' — which is what the GQ
        button sends — put nothing on the panel at all. Note the missing full
        stop on the first; both forms allow it optionally rather than betting
        on which one arrives.

        The count differs in meaning and it does not matter: 'gq check' reports
        what is LEFT and 'gq info' what the quest asked for, and a fresh read
        starts the counter at zero either way, so both say "this many to go".

        What is in the brackets is a ROOM, not an area — "(Center Stage)",
        "(Vafprounir's Home)". target_rows already resolves a room name to the
        area it belongs to, the same as it does for campaigns.
    ]]
    trig.gqStill = addTrigger("^You still have to kill (\\d+) \\* (.+) \\((.+)\\)\\.?$",
        function(a, b, w)
            local need = trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b))
            local mob  = trim(cap3(a, w, 2, b))
            local area = trim(cap3(a, w, 3, b))
            if mob == "" then return end

            begin_gq()
            add_target("gquest", mob, area, tonumber(need) or 1)
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        Which global quest this is. Several run at once and the win
        announcement names the number, so this is the only way to know that a
        win was for the one you are in rather than somebody else's.

            Quest Name.........: [ Global quest # 2393 ]
    ]]
    --[[
            Quest Duration.....: [   81 ]
            Time Remaining.....: [   80 ]
            Time to Start......: [    2 ]

        Ticks, all of them. Read here and decremented on comm.tick, so the
        number on the tab stays true between one 'gq info' and the next.
    ]]
    trig.gqLeft = addTrigger("^Time Remaining\\s*\\.*:\\s*\\[\\s*(\\d+)",
        function(a, b, w)
            gqLeft  = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            gqStart = nil
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.gqStart = addTrigger("^Time to Start\\s*\\.*:\\s*\\[\\s*(\\d+)",
        function(a, b, w)
            gqStart = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            gqLeft  = nil
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.gqNum = addTrigger("^Quest Name\\.*:\\s*\\[\\s*Global quest # (\\d+)",
        function(a, b, w)
            local n = tonumber(trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b)))
            if n then gqNum = n end
        end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.gqTarget = addTrigger("^Kill at least (\\d+) \\* (.+) \\((.+)\\)\\.?$", function(a, b, w)
        local need = trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b))
        local mob  = trim(cap3(a, w, 2, b))
        local area = trim(cap3(a, w, 3, b))
        if mob == "" then return end

        begin_gq()
        add_target("gquest", mob, area, tonumber(need) or 1)
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        Who just died. Anything that names a freshly dead mob feeds tick_off;
        the confirmation itself never does.
    ]]
    --[[
        Off the trigger's own CAPTURE, not by matching the line again.

        Every pattern below captures the mob as group 1, so the regex engine
        has already done this work — re-doing it with string.match meant
        writing the expression twice and getting one of them wrong. It is also
        note 7: those are JS regexes, so '\\S' and '(?:a|b)' mean nothing to
        Lua, and a re-match is silently empty anywhere that is not the client.

        WHICH LINE matters as much as the pattern. The death line comes first:

            A hunting party crumbles as they are battered to death!!
            You don't receive 39 experience points.
            Congratulations, that was one of your CAMPAIGN mobs!   <-- fires
            You get 10 gold coins from the battered corpse of a hunting party.

        The confirmation lands BEFORE the corpse lines, so a lastDead fed only
        by those is empty or left over from the previous kill when the panel
        asks who died. tick_off then falls through to "first one not done" in
        STORAGE order and crosses off a row you were not even looking at.
    ]]
    local function note_dead(a, w, b)
        local who = trim(cap3(a, w, 1, b))
        if who ~= "" then lastDead = who end
    end

    trig.deadBlow  = addTrigger(
        "^(.+?) \\S+ as (?:it is|they are|he is|she is) .+ to death!+$",
        note_dead, { type = "regex" })
    trig.deadName  = addTrigger("^(.+) is DEAD!+$", note_dead, { type = "regex" })
    trig.deadAbs   = addTrigger("^You absorb the .*corpse of (.+) as magical energy\\.$",
        note_dead, { type = "regex" })
    trig.deadCorpse = addTrigger("^You get .+ from the .*corpse of (.+)\\.$",
        note_dead, { type = "regex" })
    trig.deadGold  = addTrigger(
        "^The .+ gives you .+ for the .*corpse of (.+)\\.$",
        note_dead, { type = "regex" })

    trig.campKill = addTrigger("^Congratulations, that was one of your CAMPAIGN mobs!$", function()
        local hit = tick_off("campaign", lastDead)
        lastDead = nil
        if hit then
            local room, id, zone = here()
            if id and id > 0 then see(hit.mob, room, id, zone, true) end
        end
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.gqKill = addTrigger("^Congratulations, that was one of the GLOBAL QUEST mobs!$", function()
        local gqHit = tick_off("gquest", lastDead)
        lastDead = nil
        if gqHit then
            local gqRoom, gqId, gqZone = here()
            if gqId and gqId > 0 then see(gqHit.mob, gqRoom, gqId, gqZone, true) end
        end
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        GMCP owns the quest clocks, but it only speaks when something changes —
        anything that happened before this plugin loaded is invisible to it.
        These two lines are the ones the logs settle, so they set the clock
        outright rather than waiting for a packet that may never come.

            Alex, the Taskmaster tells you 'You have 50 minutes to complete your quest.'
            [*Daily Blessing*] [5324/5324hp 3679/3679mn 4440/4440mv 50qt 418tnl] >

        50 minutes, 50qt on the prompt, three separate grants agreeing.
    ]]
    trig.qGrant = addTrigger("tells you 'You have (\\d+) minutes to complete your quest\\.'", function(a, b)
        local qline = as_text(a, b)
        if not qline then return end

        local mins = num(string.match(qline, "You have (\\d+) minutes"))
        if not mins then return end

        quest.deadline = getCurrentTime() + (mins * 60000)
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    trig.qReady = addTrigger("^(?:You do not have to wait to go on another quest\\.|QUEST: You may now quest again\\.)",
        function()
            quest.readyAt = getCurrentTime()
            quest.rang = nil
            render()
        end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        The kill only ends the hunting half. Aardwolf wants you back at the
        questmaster, and the status reply stops naming a target the moment the
        mob dies — so without this the panel goes blank at exactly the point
        the reminder is the useful thing on it.
    ]]
    trig.qKilled = addTrigger("^QUEST: You have almost completed your QUEST!", function()
        quest.turnin = true
        for _, t in ipairs(targets.quest or {}) do t.done = true end
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    --[[
        Backstop for the turn-in. GMCP's 'comp' is the real signal and carries
        the cooldown, so this only fires when that never arrived — the turnin
        guard is what keeps it from wiping a readyAt 'comp' just set.
    ]]
    trig.qComp = addTrigger("tells you 'Congratulations, .+, on completing your quest!'", function()
        if quest.turnin ~= true then return end

        clear("quest")
        quest = {}
        render()
    end, { type = "regex" })

    -- scan lines and damage messages are how the database grows
    trig.scan = addTrigger("^\\s*(?:\\((?:[^)]*)\\)\\s*)*(.+?)\\s+is (?:standing|sitting|resting|sleeping|fighting|here)",
        on_scan, { type = "regex" })

    trig.damage = addTrigger("\\b(?:destroys|massacres|slaughters|obliterates|annihilates|eviscerates|hits|misses|scratches|grazes|wounds|maims|mauls|decimates|devastates|dismembers|pulverizes)\\b\\s*(?:[^\\w\\s]+\\s*)*(\\S[^!.]*?)\\s*[!.] \\[\\d+\\]$",
        on_damage, { type = "regex" })
end
