function init()
    --[[
        Declare the GMCP we need. Core owns Core.Supports.Set — it replaces
        the server's record rather than merging, so only one plugin may send
        it — and builds the union from these. Needs: comm.quest for the quest
        target, room.info to record sightings, and Char for your LEVEL.

        Char was missing, and it took the room disambiguation down with it
        silently. Two areas hold a room called 'Deep in the Forest'; the one
        that fits your level is supposed to win — but char.status never
        arrived, so the level was nil, every candidate scored an equal zero,
        and whichever the map happened to return first was picked. The test
        passed all along because the test handed it a level.
    ]]
    broadcastPlugin("aw-gmcp", "Comm,Room,Char")

    widget = createWidget({
        type     = "html",
        name     = "snd",
        title    = "Search & Destroy",
        position = { x = 1180, y = 500 },
        size     = { width = 420, height = 320 },
        --[[
            No title bar. Every panel here draws its own header with its own
            controls, so the client's chrome was a second title above ours
            saying the same thing.

            This is a plugin DEFAULT, not a lock — it's declared through the
            appearance table at creation, which the user can still override in
            the widget's own cog. autoHideSettingsCog keeps that cog reachable
            on hover rather than it going away with the bar.
        ]]
        appearance = {
            showTitleBar        = false,
            autoHideSettingsCog = true,
        },
    })

    local saved = loadTable("aw_snd")
    if type(saved) ~= "table" then
        local raw = recall("aw_snd")
        if raw then
            local ok, data = pcall(json.decode, raw)
            if ok and type(data) == "table" then saved = data end
        end
    end

    if type(saved) == "table" then
        if saved.scan    ~= nil then cfg.scan    = saved.scan and true or false end
        if saved.rewrite ~= nil then cfg.rewrite = saved.rewrite and true or false end
        if saved.hidedone ~= nil then cfg.hidedone = saved.hidedone and true or false end
    end

    --[[
        Areas and keywords are static reference data and load every time.
        They used to sit behind the mob-database guard, so the moment a saved
        database existed they stopped loading entirely — which is why runto
        couldn't find a keyword for anything after the first session.
    ]]
    seed_reference()

    -- the keywords a 'where' walk has already proved, so kill does not guess
    kw_load()

    -- what we knew at logout, back before the first paint. Campaign and gquest
    -- targets only arrive when you ask for them, so without this a reload
    -- mid-campaign shows an empty panel until you remember to type 'cp check'.
    load_targets()

    --[[
        The backups are only written on save, so a fresh install has none until
        something changes. Targets are cheap to write outright; the mob database
        is not, so it's only forced when there's no backup there yet.
    ]]
    pcall(save_targets)
    if recall(DB_FILE) == nil then dirty = true end

    if not load_db() then
        local n = seed_mobs()
        if n > 0 then
            utilprint(TAG .. "seeded " .. commas(n) .. " sightings from the Mudlet database.")
            save_db()
        end
    end

    onGMCPUpdate("comm.quest", on_quest)

    --[[
        Redraw when you change AREA, not when you change room.

        GO is only offered for the area you are standing in, so walking through
        the door is the moment the row gains a button — and nothing else was
        going to repaint it. room.info fires on every step, and a full render
        per step to notice a boundary you cross once is the wrong trade, so
        this only fires on the transition.
    ]]
    local lastZone = nil
    local function on_room()
        local r = gmcp_get({ "room.info", "Room.Info" })
        if type(r) ~= "table" then return end

        local zone = str(r.zone)
        if zone == nil or zone == lastZone then return end

        lastZone = zone

        -- arriving is what a queued 'where' has been waiting for
        where_on_arrival(string.lower(trim(zone)))
        render()
    end

    --[[
        'where' answers for the current area only, so both halves of the walk
        hang off knowing which area that is.

        The hit pattern is deliberately loose — two or more spaces between two
        non-blank runs — because a mob name can hold anything and so can a room
        name. It is safe only because it does nothing unless a walk of ours is
        live, and keepEvaluating so it never eats a line from anything else.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^(\\S.*?)\\s{2,}(\\S.*?)\\s*$", on_where_hit,
        { type = "regex", priority = 40, keepEvaluating = true })

    addTrigger("^There is no .+ around here\\.$", on_where_none,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You (?:don't|do not) see .+ here\\.$", on_where_none,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })

    onGMCPUpdate("room.info", on_room)
    onGMCPUpdate("Room.Info", on_room)

    --[[
        Redraw when your level lands.

        Rows drawn before char.status arrives have no area on them at all now,
        because guessing without a level is what put a lowbie target in a level
        200 zone. This is what turns them into real rows a moment later, and it
        is also what fixes them after a level up moves you into a different
        area's range.
    ]]
    local lastLvl = nil
    local function on_level()
        local n = my_level()
        if n and n ~= lastLvl then
            lastLvl  = n
            roomArea = {}      -- picks were scored against the old level
            render()
        end
    end

    --[[
        One tick of the MUD's clock. A global quest measures itself in these,
        so this is the only honest way to keep its numbers current without
        asking 'gq info' over and over.
    ]]
    onGMCPUpdate("comm.tick", function()
        --[[
            Learn the tick from the tick. A running average rather than the
            last gap, so one slow packet does not become the new truth.
        ]]
        local at = getCurrentTime()
        if num(tickLast) then
            local gap = at - tickLast
            if gap > 10000 and gap < 120000 then
                tickMs = math.floor((tickMs * 3 + gap) / 4)
            end
        end
        tickLast = at

        local moved = false

        if num(gqStart) and gqStart > 0 then
            gqStart = gqStart - 1
            if gqStart <= 0 then gqStart = nil end
            moved = true
        elseif num(gqLeft) and gqLeft > 0 then
            gqLeft = gqLeft - 1
            if gqLeft <= 0 then gqLeft = nil end
            moved = true
        end

        if moved then render() end
    end)

    onGMCPUpdate("char.status", on_level)
    onGMCPUpdate("Char.Status", on_level)
    arm()

    --[[
        A reload mid-quest starts blank otherwise, so ask. Ask, specifically —
        reading getGMCPData("comm.quest") instead resurrected quests that had
        been turned in an hour earlier, because that store holds the last thing
        the package ever said and not the current state. The reply to this is a
        fresh status packet, which is the only version that's true.

        1500ms because Core defers its supports rebuild ~700ms after a plugin
        enables, and Comm has to be subscribed before the reply can arrive.
    ]]
    setTimeout(function()
        sendGMCP("request quest")
    end, 1500)

    --[[
        Clear first. init() runs again on every hot-reload and
        registerWidgetEvent APPENDS — so each reload stacks another handler on
        the same widget and one click fires all of them. It shows up as buttons
        sending their command two, three, five times, getting worse the longer
        a session goes on, and nothing about it looks like a plugin bug from
        the outside.

        unregisterWidgetEvent with no callback drops every handler for the
        event, which is exactly what a fresh init wants.
    ]]
    drop_handlers(widget, "action")
    registerWidgetEvent(widget, "action", function(data)
        if type(data) ~= "table" then return end

        local act = tostring(data.action or "")
        local arg = tostring(data.data or "")

        if act == "tab" then
            view = "targets"
            tab  = arg

        elseif act == "view" then
            view = (arg == "mobs") and "mobs" or "targets"

        elseif act == "go" then
            -- an index into the rows as last drawn, or a bare vnum from the
            -- mob list, which has no area to offer anyway
            local row = goRows[tonumber(arg) or -1]
            if row then
                go(row.vnum, row.area)
            else
                go(arg)
            end
            return

        elseif act == "runto" then
            --[[
                An index off the row, or a bare area name. The mob list's own
                runto has no target to look for and passes the area straight
                through, same as GO does.
            ]]
            local row = runRows[tonumber(arg) or -1]
            if row then
                run_and_where(row.area, row.mob)
            else
                runto(arg)
            end
            return

        elseif act == "where" then
            where_start(arg)
            return

        elseif act == "hunt" then
            hunt_start(arg)
            return

        elseif act == "trick" then
            trick_start(arg)
            return

        elseif act == "refresh" then
            refresh_tab(arg)
            return

        elseif act == "qcomplete" then
            send("quest complete")
            return

        elseif act == "qrequest" then
            send("quest request")
            return

        elseif act == "gqjoin" then
            send("gquest join " .. (tonumber(arg) or ""))
            return

        elseif act == "kill" then
            send("kill " .. kw_for(arg))
            return

        elseif act == "target" then
            -- selecting a target looks it up in the database
            -- [a-z]/[0-9], not %a/%d: these run through a JS regex engine
            local kind, idx = string.match(arg, "^([a-z]+):([0-9]+)$")
            local t = kind and targets[kind] and targets[kind][tonumber(idx)]
            if t then
                lookup = where(t.mob)
                view   = "mobs"
            end

        else
            return
        end

        render()
    end)

    -- sightings accumulate constantly; flushing on a timer beats writing the
    -- whole database on every scan line
    addTimer(30000, save_db, true)

    --[[
        One-second clock. setBoundValue writes into the marked span rather
        than re-rendering, so this costs a string push instead of rebuilding
        the panel sixty times a minute.
    ]]
    addTimer(1000, function()
        if not widget then return end

        local txt, state = quest_clock()

        local cleft = camp_clock()
        if cleft then setBoundValue(widget, "cpclock", long_clock(cleft)) end

        if txt then
            setBoundValue(widget, "qclock", txt)
            setBoundValue(widget, "qtab", txt)
        elseif state == "ready" and quest.rang ~= true then
            quest.rang = true          -- cooldown just ran out; redraw once
            render()
        end
    end, true)

    --[[
        The clock is interpolated between packets, so it drifts. Ask the MUD
        every five minutes and take its number as the truth — cheap, and it
        also recovers a panel whose state was lost to a reload.
    ]]
    addTimer(300000, function()
        sendGMCP("request quest")
    end, true)

    render()
end

function cleanup()
    save_db()
    pcall(save_targets)
end

registerCommand("snd", function(args)
    local a   = argv(args)
    local sub = a[1] and string.lower(a[1]) or ""

    if sub == "" then
        utilprint(TAG .. commas(rows()) .. " sightings, " .. commas(count(mobs)) .. " mobs, "
            .. commas(count(areas)) .. " areas")
        utilprint("$w  snd cp | quest | gq     ask the MUD for that list")
        utilprint("$w  snd go <roomid>         walk there")
    utilprint("$w  snd runto <area>        let the MUD run you to an area")
    utilprint("$w  snd areas [text]        area list with keywords and levels")
        utilprint("$w  snd scan on|off         learn mobs from room descriptions")
        utilprint("$w  snd hidedone on|off     drop finished targets, or keep them listed")
        utilprint("$w  snd where <mob>         ask which rooms it is in HERE, and remember them")
        utilprint("$w  snd why                 how each row decided which area it is in")
        utilprint("$w  snd save                flush the database now")
        utilprint("$w  mobwhere <name>         everywhere it has been seen")
    utilprint("$w  ah <mob> / aha          auto-hunt, and cancel")
    utilprint("$w  ht [mob]                hunt trick on a campaign target")
        return
    end

    if sub == "cp"    then send("cp check")   return end
    if sub == "quest" then refresh_tab("quest") return end
    if sub == "gq"    then send("gq check")   return end

    if sub == "go" then
        --[[
            A bare number is a position in the visible list, which is what the
            numbering is for. Anything larger is treated as a room id.
        ]]
        local n = tonumber(a[2])
        local list = targets[tab] or {}

        if n and n >= 1 and n <= #list then
            local t = list[n]
            local hits = where(t.mob)

            if #hits > 0 and hits[1].roomid > 0 and roomExists(hits[1].roomid) then
                go(hits[1].roomid, t.area)
            else
                runto(t.area ~= "" and t.area or (hits[1] and hits[1].zone) or "")
            end
            return
        end

        go(a[2])
        return
    end

    --[[
        How each row decided which area it is in.

        Three rounds went into "it shows the wrong area" on guesswork, because
        the panel prints a conclusion and nothing about how it got there —
        there are four ways a row can arrive at an area and they fail
        differently. This prints the workings.
    ]]
    if sub == "why" then
        local list = targets[tab] or {}
        if #list == 0 then utilprint(TAGR .. "no " .. tab .. " targets") return end

        utilprint(TAG .. "standing in $C" .. tostring(here_area() or "?") .. "$w")

        for i, t in ipairs(list) do
            local raw  = t.area or ""
            local key  = area_key(raw)
            local hits = where(t.mob)
            local dest = (#hits > 0) and hits[1] or nil

            local zones = {}
            for _, h in ipairs(hits) do
                if str(h.zone) then zones[string.lower(trim(h.zone))] = true end
            end

            local room = (key == nil) and area_of_room(raw, zones) or nil

            utilprint("$K " .. i .. ". $w" .. t.mob)
            utilprint("$K      MUD said: $w" .. (raw ~= "" and raw or "(nothing)"))
            utilprint("$K      area_key: $w" .. tostring(key))
            utilprint("$K      as a room: $w"
                .. (room and (tostring(room.name) .. " $K(key=" .. tostring(room.key)
                    .. " vnum=" .. tostring(room.vnum) .. ")$w") or "no"))
            utilprint("$K      sightings: $w" .. #hits
                .. (dest and ("  $Kfirst=" .. tostring(dest.room)
                    .. " zone=" .. tostring(dest.zone)
                    .. " id=" .. tostring(dest.roomid) .. "$w") or ""))
            utilprint("$K      keyword: $w" .. kw_for(t.mob))
        end
        return
    end

    --[[
        The walk on its own, without a runto in front of it. Standing in an
        area and wanting it in the database is a thing you do while learning
        one, and it is how this got tested.
    ]]
    if sub == "where" then
        local mobName = ""
        for i = 2, #a do mobName = mobName .. (mobName == "" and "" or " ") .. a[i] end

        if mobName == "" then
            utilprint(TAGR .. "snd where <mob>   - ask which rooms it is in here, and remember them")
            return
        end

        where_start(mobName)
        return
    end

    if sub == "areas" then
        utilprint(TAG .. commas(count(areas)) .. " areas, " .. commas(count(keywords)) .. " keyword exceptions")

        local q = string.lower(trim(a[2] or ""))
        local shown = 0

        for name, rec in pairs(areas) do
            if q == "" or string.find(name, q, 1, true) then
                utilprint("$w  " .. (rec.name or name) .. " $Y(" .. tostring(rec.key) .. ")$w  "
                    .. tostring(rec.minlvl) .. "-" .. tostring(rec.maxlvl))
                shown = shown + 1
                if shown >= 20 then
                    utilprint("$w  ...")
                    break
                end
            end
        end

        if shown == 0 then utilprint(TAGR .. "no area matching '" .. q .. "'") end
        return
    end

    if sub == "runto" then
        -- built by hand: table.concat's start-index form is not something to
        -- assume survives a reimplemented stdlib
        local rest = {}
        for i = 2, #a do table.insert(rest, a[i]) end
        runto(table.concat(rest, " "))
        return
    end

    if sub == "scan" then
        cfg.scan = (a[2] or "on") ~= "off"
        saveTable("aw_snd", cfg)
        keep("aw_snd", cfg)
        utilprint(TAG .. "scan learning " .. (cfg.scan and "on" or "off"))
        return
    end

    --[[
        Finished targets sink to the bottom either way. This decides whether
        they stay there at all — worth having both, because a crossed-off row
        is a record of what you already did on a long campaign, and clutter on
        a gquest you are working through.
    ]]
    if sub == "hidedone" or sub == "done" then
        cfg.hidedone = (a[2] or "on") ~= "off"
        saveTable("aw_snd", cfg)
        keep("aw_snd", cfg)
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.hidedone
            and "finished targets are removed from the list."
            or  "finished targets stay on the list, at the bottom."))
        return
    end

    if sub == "save" then
        dirty = true
        save_db()
        utilprint(TAG .. "saved " .. commas(rows()) .. " sightings.")
        return
    end

    utilprint(TAGR .. "unknown option '" .. sub .. "' — /snd for help")
end, "Search and Destroy: targets, mob lookup and walking")

    for i = 1, #a do table.insert(rest, a[i]) end
    trick_start(table.concat(rest, " "))
end, "Hunt trick: walk hunt <n>.<keyword> until the MUD refuses, which marks the campaign target")

registerCommand("ah", function(args)
    local a = argv(args)
    local rest = {}
    for i = 1, #a do table.insert(rest, a[i]) end
    hunt_start(table.concat(rest, " "))
end, "Auto-hunt: follow the hunt skill to a mob")

registerCommand("aha", function()
    hunt_stop("cancelled")
    trick_stop("cancelled")
end, "Cancel an auto-hunt or hunt trick")

registerCommand("mobwhere", function(args)
    local a = argv(args)
    local q = table.concat(a, " ")

    if trim(q) == "" then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "mobwhere <name>")
        return
    end

    lookup = where(q)
    view   = "mobs"
    render()

    if #lookup == 0 then
        utilprint(TAGR .. "never seen '" .. q .. "'.")
        return
    end

    utilprint(TAG .. #lookup .. " sighting(s) for '" .. q .. "':")
    for i, h in ipairs(lookup) do
        if i > 8 then break end
        utilprint("$w  " .. h.room .. " $Y(" .. h.zone .. ")$w  " .. h.seen .. "x  #" .. h.roomid)
    end
end, "Every room a mob has been seen in")
